text:
I declare open his hearing of the Environment and Communications Legislation Committee into the 2026-27 budget estimates. I begin by acknowledging the traditional custodians of the land on which we meet and pay respects to elders past, present and emerging. The committee has fixed Thursday 17 December 2026 as the date for the return of answers to questions taken on notice. The committee's proceedings today will begin with the corporate matters and general questions aspect of the communications, sport and the arts portfolio. Under standing order 26, the committee must take all evidence in public session, and this includes answers to questions on notice. I remind all witnesses that, in giving evidence to the committee, they are protected by parliamentary privilege. It is unlawful for anyone to threaten or disadvantage a witness on account of evidence given to a committee, and such action may be treated by the Senate as contempt. It is also a contempt to give false or misleading evidence.

Senators endorsed the following test of relevance of questions at estimates hearings. Any questions going to the operations or financial positions of the departments or agencies which are seeking funds in estimates are relevant for the purposes of estimates hearings. I remind officers that the Senate has resolved that there are no areas in connection with the expenditure of public funds where any person has a discretion to withhold details or explanations from the parliament or its committees unless the parliament has expressly provided otherwise. The Senate has also resolved that an officer of a department of the Commonwealth should not be asked to give opinions on matters of policy and shall be given reasonable opportunity to refer questions asked of the officer to superior officers or to a minister. This resolution does not preclude questions asking for explanations of policies or factual questions about when and how policies were adopted.

Witnesses are reminded of the Senate order specifying the process by which a claim of public interest immunity should be raised. I incorporate the public interest immunity statement into the Hansard.

The extract read as follows—

Public interest immunity claims

That the Senate—

(a) notes that ministers and officers have continued to refuse to provide information to Senate committees without properly raising claims of public interest immunity as required by past resolutions of the Senate;

(b) reaffirms the principles of past resolutions of the Senate by this order, to provide ministers and officers with guidance as to the proper process for raising public interest immunity claims and to consolidate those past resolutions of the Senate;

(c) orders that the following operate as an order of continuing effect:

(1) If:

(a) a Senate committee, or a senator in the course of proceedings of a committee, requests information or a document from a Commonwealth department or agency; and

(b) an officer of the department or agency to whom the request is directed believes that it may not be in the public interest to disclose the information or document to the committee, the officer shall state to the committee the ground on which the officer believes that it may not be in the public interest to disclose the information or document to the committee, and specify the harm to the public interest that could result from the disclosure of the information or document.

(2) If, after receiving the officer's statement under paragraph (1), the committee or the senator requests the officer to refer the question of the disclosure of the information or document to a responsible minister, the officer shall refer that question to the minister.

(3) If a minister, on a reference by an officer under paragraph (2), concludes that it would not be in the public interest to disclose the information or document to the committee, the minister shall provide to the committee a statement of the ground for that conclusion, specifying the harm to the public interest that could result from the disclosure of the information or document.

(4) A minister, in a statement under paragraph (3), shall indicate whether the harm to the public interest that could result from the disclosure of the information or document to the committee could result only from the publication of the information or document by the committee, or could result, equally or in part, from the disclosure of the information or document to the committee as in camera evidence.

(5) If, after considering a statement by a minister provided under paragraph (3), the committee concludes that the statement does not sufficiently justify the withholding of the information or document from the committee, the committee shall report the matter to the Senate.

(6) A decision by a committee not to report a matter to the Senate under paragraph (5) does not prevent a senator from raising the matter in the Senate in accordance with other procedures of the Senate.

(7) A statement that information or a document is not published, or is confidential, or consists of advice to, or internal deliberations of, government, in the absence of specification of the harm to the public interest that could result from the disclosure of the information or document, is not a statement that meets the requirements of paragraph (1) or (4).

(8) If a minister concludes that a statement under paragraph (3) should more appropriately be made by the head of an agency, by reason of the independence of that agency from ministerial direction or control, the minister shall inform the committee of that conclusion and the reason for that conclusion, and shall refer the matter to the head of the agency, who shall then be required to provide a statement in accordance with paragraph (3).

(d) requires the Procedure Committee to review the operation of this order and report to the Senate by 20 August 2009.

(13 May 2009 J.1941)

(Extract, Senate Standing Orders)

text:
Senators are aware that one of the roles of the committee chair is to ensure that proceedings are conducted in an orderly and civil way. This is not intended to prevent rigorous questioning of witnesses, but to help ensure that senators exercise their rights and privileges in a careful, civil, polite and responsible manner. I remind senators of their obligations under the Behaviour Code for Australian Parliamentarians to treat witnesses with dignity, courtesy, fairness and respect and, as chair, I intend to uphold these standards.

Senators are also reminded that questions relating to a bill may be asked during estimates where they concern only the operations, administration or financial position of a department or agency. Questions about the meaning, purpose, intention or effect of specific provisions of a bill that is subject of a separate Senate inquiry should be pursued through that inquiry process rather than during estimates hearings.

These are public proceedings being video streamed live via the parliament's website and a Hansard transcript is being made. If there are no objections, the committee authorises media recording and photography of the committee's proceedings in accordance with broadcasting resolution 3. I remind any media present during the day that this permission can be revoked at any time, and the media must follow the direction of secretariat staff.

text:
I'm not sure that's an entirely accurate characterisation. I think what the Secretaries Board was seeking was that broadcasts of proceedings of a committee, including excerpts from committee proceedings, should be for the purpose only of making fair and accurate reports of those proceedings, which is a pre-existing policy of the Senate. The first thing that the Secretaries Board did in its submission was to state clearly that it strongly supported parliamentary accountability, transparency and robust scrutiny. However, it was an inquiry by the joint committee on parliamentary standards which invited submissions from interested parties. Having spent 12 hours in Senate estimates yesterday, I think I am an interested party, as are other secretaries.

Our concern—and I know that there is concern among parliamentarians as well—is that sometimes behaviour in the parliament doesn't meet the standards that parliament has set for itself. The chair has been very vigilant in making sure that that is spelled out, including this morning with his references to dignity, courtesy, fairness and respect. We are simply very conscious as employers and accountable authorities that for many of our staff, if they were exposed to that behaviour, it might compromise their safety in the workplace or their feelings of psychosocial safety. And so we felt it was incumbent on us to make a representation to that committee inquiry, recognising that it is always for the parliament to set its policies and that nothing that the Secretaries Board is seeking to do is more than to bring legitimate concerns to the attention of the parliament so that it can take those into account as it makes policy.

text: Mr Betts, I'm going to ask if you could provide, on notice, your draft comments to that Secretaries Board correspondence, because the ability for the Senate to do its job in Senate estimates, including this committee, is very important, and being able to highlight on social media, using the vision which is made available through the parliament, is a fundamental function of this committee, I would put to you. portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
Well, the Senate has. I would merely point out that, certainly in the case of the committee I was in yesterday, there is 14 hours of footage which is already in the public domain from there, so there's no attempt to frustrate the Senate's ability to do its job. The concern that was expressed by the Secretaries Board was about the very selective editing of those videos and the overlay of commentary and captions which were designed to humiliate public servants, unfairly and inconsistently with the Senate's own resolutions. I'm sure you wouldn't support that.

What we also find—and this is particularly true for female public servants—is that the comments sections on websites hosted by senators and other parliamentarians contain often vile and misogynistic comments about female public servants. We felt it was incumbent on us to point out to the parliament that that was creating unacceptable levels of exposure for our people and that the parliament should take that seriously and consider whether it needed to take remedial action.

text: One of the issues that were raised was the video that I posted with Mr Collette. I properly questioned Mr Collette over a decision he made to fund someone who is a known antisemite, Mr Matt Chun, who wrote an essay following the massacre at Bondi saying, 'We don't mourn fascists.' I simply asked him to disavow the conduct of someone that Creative Australia had funded. It was one of the most horrific things anyone could write following Bondi. Mr Collette took exception to me posting that video. It's completely inappropriate that he cannot see that to fund someone like that, Mr Betts—now, if he wants to take a different view, that is up to him. But, as a senator, I'm entitled to raise serious concerns, because we have seen systemic funding of people who prosecute hate in this country through media grants, through Creative Australia and through various other multicultural grants. If Mr Collette has a problem with the way that I have highlighted his failure to disavow the decision that Creative Australia made, can I say to you that perhaps he's in the wrong job.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Okay. I thought we were talking about the Secretaries Board submission to the parliamentary inquiry about respectful behaviour in Senate estimates. You and I have had a number of discussions, Senator, which have been respectful discussions, around the need to tackle antisemitism in this country and some of the often difficult public policy judgements that need to be made about, on the one hand, protecting the Jewish community in this country from antisemitic hatred and, on the other hand, the need to protect freedom of speech. text: Thank you. My questions once again relate to the review of Australia's classification system. We've been on this for some time. Last estimates, I asked about written material and kept on getting answers relating to other media as well. Can we save time today and just limit your answer to written material, please? That's what I'm after. The review of the classification system started in 2019 with the Stevens review. Legislation inspired by the Stevens review occurred in 2024, five years later. Then the current review started into the issues Stevens raised but did not resolve. It's now 2026. This whole process continues at what seems to me to be a snail's pace. Public consultation on the measures you expect to take was completed in May. It's now October. Minister, what is the time line for completing the review and making our classification system fit for purpose? When will you finish it?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Periodically and over a successive number of budgets, the government has decided to seek savings from departments by requiring them to reduce expenditure on non-staff items, consultants, contractors, legal expenses and travel. text: What is the routine or mechanism inside the department when travel is approved? I'm assuming that—do people have to give a certain number of days' notice for travel? portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There are policies in place, which are whole-of-government policies specified by the Department of Finance, that we are required to comply with, including the use of centralised service providers and rules around ensuring value for money through the appropriate fare. Sometimes the availability of that fare will depend on timing, it will depend on destination and so on, but I'll ask the team to take you through more detail.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We do have detailed policy, but we also have detailed guidance as well to provide additional information to support officials booking travel. Officials are encouraged to book travel as soon as possible, so as early as possible. We do obviously acknowledge that there are often circumstances which require that travel to happen quite urgently. In all cases, we do require staff to seek a number of quotes. That is available to be done through the whole-of-government travel system, CTM. We ask staff to look across the panel airlines that are available through CTM to ensure that they've got a number of different flight options. They are required to seek the best value fare under the whole-of-Australian-government framework. That doesn't necessarily mean the cheapest flight. There are other things that need to be taken into consideration, but price is one of those key drivers. That is required to be documented when they put in their approval for travel so that the delegate's able to look at what the different arrangements are and the different considerations that have been made to meet that best value framework.

So we're pretty much in alignment with the market share as between Qantas, Virgin and other airlines. That's been true over a number of years now. We are routinely asked about this in the RRAT committee under the transport outcome.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And that experience for this department is uniform across government?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But you obviously do the research. You obviously go to RRAT and—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When it comes to accommodation for officials, how is that arranged or organised?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Do you have any information in terms of what forward travel is anticipated for the department?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Any international travel by the minister would require approval from the Prime Minister. Notwithstanding her participation in the recent event in Papua New Guinea, I'm not aware of the minister having any approved forward international travel, but we'll need to just check that.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The formal mechanism for seeking the Prime Minister's approval for international travel—is that handled by the department or by the minister's office?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The minister's—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's handled by the minister's office?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: A letter or document is produced, and then it's approved by the Prime Minister.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And does the department provide any input into that letter?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sometimes we may. It's worth saying, just for the complete avoidance of doubt, there may be events which are forthcoming in the international calendar—for instance, the International Telecommunications Union—where we may prospectively and in a preliminary way book flights, for instance, in case the minister chose to travel. But that would be subject to the Prime Minister's approval. If that approval wasn't forthcoming then those bookings would be withdrawn.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So the booking of any preliminary flights in anticipation of the minister's travel would be—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As we've said, you get better value for money sometimes when you book it. So sometimes on a precautionary basis we'll make a tentative booking, but the travel is not locked in until it's approved by the Prime Minister. We can provide you with a bit more detail around that process.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Does the Prime Minister have to approve the booking of preliminary flights?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Where the minister may—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: choose to or may choose not to.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Has advice been provided to the minister, Mr Betts?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

text: What are you taking on notice for me, Minister?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

text: So no preliminary—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm looking through the prospective, and you've taken that on notice.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Between the department and the minister's office, we'll make sure you've got that list of events that are considered over the next forward program.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We do have some responses to the questions on most popular destinations or most frequent destinations.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: First Assistant Secretary and Chief Financial Officer

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As it relates to domestic travel, the most popular or currently travelled—
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I wouldn't use the word 'popular'.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Frequently travelled.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Work-orientated destinations.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The most frequently travelled domestic routes firstly relate to the territories, so that covers Norfolk, Christmas and Cocos Islands. That's 18 per cent of domestic flights in 2025-26. Then Canberra to Melbourne is 17 per cent, Canberra to Sydney is 15 per cent and Canberra to Brisbane is 14 per cent.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And Canberra to Perth?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I hope it comes in slightly ahead of Hobart. Okay, thank you very much.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. We've now concluded the corporate section. Based on the wishes of the committee, we will break now and come back with outcome 5.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I now call officers from the department in relation to outcome 5, Promote an innovative and competitive communication sector through policy development and advice program delivery so all Australians can realise the full potential of digital technologies and communication services; Program 5.1, Digital technologies and communication services; and Closing the Gap outcome 17, Digital inclusion.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can I again put on the record that I think the response to questions on notice due on 17 July and the fact that they've only just been lodged now during estimates is so disrespectful, not just to this committee but also to the Senate. I will be taking up the possibility of a spillover for that purpose because it's just completely unacceptable. We cannot do our job when—the government talks about transparency, Minister, and this flies in the face of everything that the government has talked about. This is one of the—as I say, this is just so disrespectful. It makes it very difficult for us to do our job properly.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is there a question, sorry, Senator?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, there is a question. I want to move to the digital duty of care. I've raised a number of very serious concerns about the proposed bill and the draft bill—the exposure draft. But I'm wanting to ask about—I'm not aware of whether—I have had a departmental briefing, so I'm aware of some of these concerns, but I want to go to the heart of why the legislated codes and standards are going to be removed from the bill after 12 months. They set out very prescriptive obligations, including obligations on digital platforms to detect, prevent and remove unlawful material such as child sexual abuse material, terrorism material and extreme violence material. They were very detailed and prescriptive obligations along with a whole range of other prescriptive obligations concerning age-restricted material. What concerns has the eSafety Commissioner raised in relation to that decision, and why have these codes, after 12 months, been removed with no guarantees that anything which obligates the platforms and other relevant online services will be required to take those proactive measures to stop this material being online in the first place?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That, I think, does go to the substance of the content of the bill, which is before a committee. The advice I've received for this estimates, and I read it out earlier, was that, while the questions relating to a bill that concern the operations, administration or financial position of the department or agency can be asked, that really goes to the core of the policy rationale and the operation of the bill itself. Questions about the meaning, purpose, intent or effect of a bill or a provision that's subject to a separate Senate inquiry should be pursued through that inquiry process rather than through the estimates hearing.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Chair, I'm asking these questions because we've seen in the past that, despite Senate inquiries undertaking their work in relation to bills, bills have also been fast-tracked through the parliament—and I refer specifically to the environmental laws—before the committee even reports. So—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, Senator—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, hold on. Let me respond to two aspects of that. First, it doesn't bring it within that relevance concern at the moment. But the second point is that, on this occasion, I think it was your motion in the Senate that set the timetable of this, so—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You voted against it.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, we may have, but—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The Greens and Labor voted against it.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: My point is that's not quite an apposite point in that respect. I would just say we're not going to go to the substance of the bill today for the reasons that I've outlined and on the basis of the advice that I've received.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I appreciate that issue. Can I ask whether the eSafety Commissioner expressed concern about the removal of the codes and standards in the bill after 12 months?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We had a number of conversations with the eSafety Commissioner and with her team. We held lengthy workshops on a number of occasions about the bill. We have worked through a lot of different aspects of the bill. We've talked about the codes and standards, and my understanding is that the commissioner is comfortable with what we've landed on.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But there is no equivalent provision within the bill. Those codes and standards have been removed, and I'm asking about—look, clearly I've had briefings with both the department and the eSafety Commissioner, so I've had some discussions about the concerns in relation to the removal of the codes and standards. Now, those briefings occurred before the release of the bill. I was expecting that they would be reinstated. They've only been reinstated for 12 months as a transition measure. So there's nothing that goes to the substantive issues that are detailed in the codes and standards. Now, I appreciate we won't get stuck in the weeds in relation to the provisions of the bill, but can you just detail the concerns the eSafety Commissioner raised in this respect to the department?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As I said, we had a number of conversations with the eSafety Commissioner. We have agreed that the bill does capture what the codes and standards capture in principle. The detail isn't there. The detail will be in the regulatory guidance that will be issued by the commissioner, and that will make it available to everybody who needs to comply and will make it more flexible and responsive to changes in technology and to emerging harms.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Could you just point me to where in the bill the regulatory—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I am not answering a question about the bill, Senator.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, no, I'm responding—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: All right, we've got two people raising hands. I think—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, Chair, can I just—sorry, I literally got cut off after two words.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Everyone needs to just come to order.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You're essentially ignoring the advice of the chair.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Give me a moment—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can I just be allowed to ask my question before you rule on it, Chair?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, hold on. The predecessor question was getting very close to that. What I will say is, as I said before, if it goes to what's in and not in the bill and the policy rationales or related matters that go to that substance then it isn't within scope. It can go to administration, spending of money, operations of the department, such as when briefings were held, but it can't go to why something was in or out of the bill or the nature of the substance of it. I'm listening very carefully to your question.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Ms Vandenbroek, there's nothing in the bill that requires the eSafety Commissioner to make regulatory guidelines to replace the online codes and standards. So I go back to my question, and I also ask for any advice or briefs or correspondence that the eSafety Commissioner provided the department in relation to the removal of the codes and standards. Did you receive advice from the eSafety Commissioner in writing in relation to this matter?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I would need to check that. We had, as I said, a lot of meetings with the commissioner and with her team. We talked through a lot of things in detail. We made a lot of notes that we then considered. I don't remember specifically whether the commissioner wrote to us about the codes and standards.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Just to make an obvious point, the eSafety Commissioner is the right person to ask about the views of the eSafety Commissioner.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Betts, I'm asking about documents in the possession of the department and the advice that you have received, and that's appropriate.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sure, but your question began with what were the views and concerns of the eSafety Commissioner, and I don't want to put my witnesses in a position where they're asked to speak on behalf of an independent regulator.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

text: The issue that I'm raising is that the minister dragged her feet for at least a week. She said nothing about this when this occurred. She did not raise any concerns for at least a week. They have a process where these things reach public ire, and I appreciate the fact that they have now referred it to the ombudsman for that to play out.' That's probably one of the very few times, Minister, that Minister Wells has raised concerns about when the ABC crosses the line in a very serious way, as it has also done in the Mahmood Fazal matter. This is the public broadcaster. It receives almost $1.3 billion of taxpayers' funding every year. Australians expect it to operate at its very best. portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Good morning. My line of questions are around the evidence that the department gave in August around the reference links in the report of the Age Assurance Technology Trial. So search and reference links in the report to the AATT were correct at the time the report was handed over but became broken later on. Now, having considered the archives that I presented to the department in questions on notice which proved the links were always incorrect, including at the time the report was handed over, does the department accept that it misled the committee on this issue?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, because the department was operating in good faith on the understanding that those citations were correct, which was the responsibility of the author of the report. The moment that it became apparent that there were typographical errors and flaws in terms of the citations, they were identified as erroneous and a corrigendum correcting all identified errors was published alongside the report on the department's website. There was no intention to mislead. The minor technical problems with those references, which in no way altered the substance of that report, were not known to us at the time that evidence was given. As soon as they became known, we corrected them and took the right action.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So the answer to the question was, no, you haven't misled the committee?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Completely correct.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's on the back of what we heard during the hearing where Ms Vandenbroek and, I think, Mr Mackay provided some evidence. In question IQ26-000102 I presented the department with archived versions of webpages which show that an article cited as Weber et al contained a digital object identifier which pointed to the wrong article in 2024, as it does now. So does the department believe that this pointed to the right article in 2025 and has changed twice in two years?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As the secretary of the department, I tend not to proofread references in technical reports. If the question is, 'Did the department mislead the Senate?' then that would require us to have knowingly presented incorrect information. Yes, there were errors in the report in terms of the six citations and a few typographical mistakes. That is not in dispute from us. My officials operated with appropriate due diligence in correcting those errors as soon as they came to light. They may wish to add more to that.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We'll add to that. We do now accept that they were not correct at the time the report was handed over, but that was not our understanding at the previous committee hearing.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So do you agree that it's changed twice in a year? Is there evidence to show that—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I'm saying that—
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: they weren't working all along.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: the links were incorrect when the report was handed to government.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There is a possibility that, because you weren't aware of it during the previous hearing, you have accidentally misled the committee.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: If, in giving evidence—and I'm speaking generally here—with the best of intentions an official is unaware of a matter which is relevant to an answer they've given, the best that they can subsequently do is act with speed to correct that on the public record. This happens periodically in Senate estimates and elsewhere. In this case, we've clearly acted to correct any errors which were on the record; therefore, I don't think this could be characterised as anybody attempting to mislead the parliament.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I guess mistakes can happen, so it's admitting that a mistake has taken place and—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Which is what a corrigendum does. It corrects.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
It shouldn't be so hard to admit and acknowledge that, based on the lack of information that the officials had, they weren't able to provide to the committee—it could've accidentally misled the committee. Again, it could be no fault of the officials, but it's the role and duty of officials to have that information at hand before coming to estimates, at least that's the expectation that we senators have. Ms Vandenbroek, in relation to this, you told the committee:

It's very difficult to go back and check what may have been replaced a year ago.

It literally took one of my staff members half an hour to pull these archives together and comprehensively debunk what you told the committee. Again, how were you unaware that ACCS's claim could be easily disproven? We expect officials to be experts in getting this information to us.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We asked ACCS about the links. We operated on good faith on what we were told by them. I wasn't aware that there was a way that we could go and check back to the situation of a year ago. I was made aware of that, and then the team went and did that work.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Why has the department taken so long to take accountability for this misleading evidence?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand Mr Betts wrote to the committee not long after the hearing once we had confirmed. We had staff go through and check all of the hundreds of links in the report so that we knew there weren't any others other than the ones that were brought to our attention. As has been said, some other minor typographical problems were found during that process. They were also corrected, but we wanted to do that in a very thorough way before we corrected the record so that we could do it once and do it comprehensively.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
Do you have anything to say in particular to the committee—I'll go to what Mr Mackay said, and hopefully that's going to resolve a lot of this. When asked in August if these errors represent lazy report writing, Mr Mackay told the committee:

I don't agree that it represents lazy report writing. If they had been broken at the time the report was finalised and provided to government then I think I would agree with you, but these are links that are now broken but were not at the time that the report was provided.

Mr Mackay, given it has now been proven the links were broken when the report was handed over, is it now your view that this is lazy report writing?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As we've covered, the secretary wrote to the committee outlining the errors that we had identified in the report and what the correct references to be included in the report were. As the secretary has noted, a corrigendum including those identified errors has been published alongside the report on the department's website. It would clearly be my expectation that reports that are provided don't contain errors, but, as the secretary set out in his correspondence to the committee, the department has acted quickly to identify the errors and to arrange for the publication of the corrigendum.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Communications, Media and Sport Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But do you agree that this is lazy report writing?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, I would expect that reports that are commissioned from suppliers to government don't contain errors. I would note that these corrected references; there are six of them in part D of the report. This is a part that that relates to emerging future technology and does not relate to anything that links through to the eSafety Commissioner's regulatory guidance. What I'm saying is that I regard these as minor errors rather than something that would change the substantive findings of the report on which the regulator has then relied.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Communications, Media and Sport Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand, but it just makes the public lose faith in the entire process if there are minor errors. I acknowledge that you've said that you guys did your best, but do you apologise to the committee for not picking up on those errors earlier?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: If it helps close this matter down then I'm happy to apologise because there were errors in a report supplied by a consultant. Total disclosure: I can't guarantee that there haven't been typos in other documents that I've been responsible for in 38 years as a public servant.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, Mr Betts. With ACCS, I note that the ATT contract required them to comply with the Commonwealth Supplier Code of Conduct, which provides that suppliers must conduct their business with integrity by acting honestly, responsibly, transparently, consistently and holding themselves accountable for their actions. Does the department believe ACCS has acted honestly?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't believe they intentionally put errors into the report, so I don't think there was any intent to be dishonest or to do anything incorrect.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So they've acted honestly in your opinion?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think the point is that they haven't acted deceptively. People make mistakes.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So the department has no issue with ACCS telling the Guardian and KJR that no AI was used in the preparation of the report, which ACCS has admitted is not true? You have no issues with ACCS causing you to mislead this committee by providing you incorrect information about the citation errors? I'm just curious to see why there's a protection racket around ACCS.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Mackay has described it as sloppy reporting. I've offered an apology to the committee to the extent that that's worthwhile. We're talking about six citations in technical footnotes related to future technology unrelated to the substance of the report which were subsequently corrected. I've written to the committee. We've put a corrigendum on our website. This isn't Watergate.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Has any action been taken against ACCS?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No. We asked them to publish the corrigendum. They hold responsibility for the website where the original report is and they published the corrigendum alongside the report. That was the extent of what we asked for.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So a contractor can lie to the department and expect to suffer no particular consequences?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I wouldn't say that they lied to us. When we met with them, the language that they used was unclear. What I took from that was that they were telling me that the citations weren't broken at the time it was handed over. They later clarified that language. It was a misunderstanding in the meeting between me and them because of the technical language that was used. So they may not have been clear in their language. I don't think that's the same thing as lying to the department.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Withholding information is very synonymous with lying, but okay. Does the department still believe it is appropriate for an internal investigation into the giving of misleading evidence to a Senate committee to take place, or is the department just hoping that something like this doesn't happen again, as Mr McKay mentioned earlier?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm satisfied that the department has taken all reasonable steps proportionate to the scale of the error.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Pocock.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I've got a bunch of questions about the government's gambling reform bill that passed. The first one was on inducements. Rather than banning inducements as was recommended by the Murphy report, the government has now changed the law to prevent gambling companies from contacting people for three months after they come off BetStop. I've been advised that gambling companies don't actually know when people have come off BetStop, as there's no way for them to see someone's deregistration date. Is that true?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I will need to take that on notice. I'm not 100 per cent sure. Apologies.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: If you can come back today, that'd be great. On the grandfathering of certain commercial deals, is it correct that the prohibition on using social media influencers to advertise gambling on social media has also been grandfathered?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The only grandfathering element in the act relates to sporting officials' uniforms.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
I'm reading directly from the bill:

Subsection 62W(1) of the new IGA Act applies in relation to a contract, arrangement or understanding entered into on or after the commencement day.

Are you sure that doesn't include influencers?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The commencement of that provision will be 1 January 2027.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But it doesn't seem like there was a prohibition on influencers doing five- or 10-year deals—or was that explicitly ruled out in the act?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There's no provision in the legislation to grandfather any provisions in relation to notable people.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Those provisions will come into effect on 1 January 2026.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And that'll then be illegal.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In line with what's provided in the legislation and then outlined in the guidance from the Australian Communications and Media Authority.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But is that 'in relation to a contract, arrangement or understanding entered into on or after the commencement day'?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Any contract entered into on or after the commencement date, being 1 January 2027, will not be valid.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, but I'm asking about grandfathering. What if someone does a deal on 30 December?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Those contracts will not be grandfathered.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So they are just null and void?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Correct.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Except for jerseys.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes—and stadiums.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I will go on to AdStop. Is the government's intention that this service will be advertised to Australians?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The act, as you are aware, provides for the wagering advertising opt-out register to give Australians a single way to opt out of receiving wagering advertising across online content services. The promotion of the service is something that we will be looking into as it is established.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There are a number of preparatory steps to be put in place before it can be commenced. The ACMA is leading the work to deliver the register. Specific questions about the architecture and the operation of that register are best directed to them.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Okay. We were told it would take a year. Do you think it's on track to be delivered next August?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Again, I think there are particular stages to that process, and that's a matter for the ACMA to speak to.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Okay. I'll come back for the ACMA. I want to turn to the costing for the gambling reform package. It was titled the Wagering advertising reform: impact analysis. It says that the department commissioned the Australian Gambling Research Centre to estimate the benefits and the costs of wagering ad reforms. I'm assuming this is the document that informed the minister in their consideration of what they would advance. The impact analysis contained three options: (1) maintain the status quo; (2) a partial ban, which, as we know, the major parties passed together; and (3) a full ban, as recommended by the Murphy report. Option 2, the one that was passed, wasn't actually modelled by the AGRC; however, the impact analysis says that the socioeconomic benefits associated with this option would be between $117.6 million and $182.2 million. Having looked at the AGRC report, I don't understand how you've come to that conclusion, so I'm really keen to understand what happened there.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There were a number of amendments to what was modelled in the AGRC report. They went in both directions. On balance, while the number of ads per hour changed, we also added in things that strengthened the protections, which were no ads on jerseys, no ads in stadiums, no promotion of odds and no use of notable people. On balance, it was agreed that that meant it could still be costed within the range for option 2, and that was an assessment that was accepted by the Office of Impact Assessment.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But both of those figures, the $117.6 million and the $182.2 million, come from options that were clearly stronger than option 2, even when you add in those little tidbits.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, could you repeat the question?
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Those figures come from options that were clearly stronger than what was ultimately passed, yet you're saying that what was passed is somewhere in there. I'm just trying to understand the sort of mathematical manipulation or sums that were done to try and get those numbers to apply to an option that was clearly much weaker than the option that the AGRC said was attached to those figures. Take the lower one, the $117.6 million. That figure assumed a complete ban on ads online, a ban during live sport and for 60 minutes either side, and a limit of two ads per hour on TV. There's no complete ban for the 60 minutes on either side, and online is some sort of opt-out system, so how are you using those numbers.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As I said, there were a lot of movements. Mr Adams might be able to add more detail than that.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can you provide the updated report, then?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, the updated—
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Report.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: From AGRC?
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We didn't have the final model costed by AGRC. There wasn't time through the development of the bill.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Okay. How did you do it then?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As Ms Vandenbroek said, there were a number of elements both ways. You've pointed out some of the elements that were stronger in the AGRC model than what we finally ended up with. But, as Ms Vandenbroek points out, there were a number of elements that were strengthened, including the ban on venues, the ban on the use of notable people and the ban on the promotion of odds, amongst other things, as well as the triple-lock system, which is effectively a ban unless someone has a triple-lock system in place, and the 15 minutes before the live sport commences and five minutes on either side. On balance, there was an assessment from the department that the estimate for the socioeconomic benefit would have fallen in between those figures, as outlined in the IA.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So we have numbers from the experts, and then the department just makes some assumptions. The $182.2 million assumes something even stronger—a complete ban on ads online, no triple lock, a 50 per cent reduction of ads on TV and a 23 per cent reduction of ads on radio—and you're trying to tell us that, somehow, the watered-down approach is equivalent, or somewhere in the middle of those two numbers. When I asked you about this on notice, you stood by it. How can you, in good faith, say that option 2 is stronger than a full ban on online ads and two ads per hour on TV when option 2 contains three ads per hour on TV and a patchy opt-out system for online ads?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That was the assessment that was made at the time based on the factors that were outlined.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Who made that assessment?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The team who were working on it at the time.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can you provide that analysis, or that modelling, please.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We'll take that on notice.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Communications, Media and Sport Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Has the government asked the department to conduct any further work on responding to or implementing any of the other recommendations from the Murphy report?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, the government has not.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So all done on Murphy. What data or research will the department monitor or commission to evaluate the results of this policy ahead of the statutory review?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's a matter that the department is starting to work through, in terms of ongoing monitoring of how implementation of the reforms is tracking. That's work we will undertake in collaboration with the ACMA. As you've flagged, there is a statutory review required after three years.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Will there be a plan for evidence generation? When can we expect something?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There will be. We haven't worked through that. We are still working through the rules that are required and the guidance and the other things that are needed before we get to implementation, and then we will start working on the plan for capturing data for the evaluation.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Has any budget been given to commission research?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In relation to implementation? Not at this time, no.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

text: I'll go back to AdStop. You don't know if it'll actually be advertised to consumers?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

text: I remember when this was going through the Senate. The crossbench tried to move amendments to ensure that the levy could actually promote BetStop. I moved that amendment. The government voted against that. The levy bill didn't say that you could use the levy for promotion. So you can use the levy for promotion of BetStop?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm sorry if I misunderstood your question. I understood you to be asking about the costs of the register.

witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Communications, Media and Sport Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No—to promote it. It's one thing to have a register, but, if people don't actually know how to access it, it's a bit pointless.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The act provides that the cost recovery will include establishment, operation, administration—
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, understood.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_position: Acting Assistant Secretary, Gambling Reforms Taskforce
