portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Ananda-Rajah.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I have some questions regarding regional resilience and coverage. I'm interested in what we're doing to improve regional resilience and coverage, particularly against the context of the fires that affected Victoria 10 months ago. As you know, those were some of the worst fires in living memory—440,000 hectares burnt. They were particularly bad in the Longwood region, where 140,000 hectares burnt, and there was a complete collapse of communications within a couple of days. There were catastrophic conditions. To say it hampered the response and recovery is an understatement. I'm interested in it, but I'm also speaking on behalf of my friend and colleague Dr Helen Haines, who's been a fierce advocate for improving regional connectivity and coverage. I was recently in that area, and it has not recovered. There are still vast mountains and hillsides that are charred and burnt. We're now going into another high-risk weather period. So I'm interested in getting an update on where implementation is at with UOMO and what's happening with temporary disaster roaming. And feel free to fill in the blanks.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
Senator, you've covered a couple of things there. In relation to the universal outdoor mobile obligation, as you know, when that takes effect—and the start date is currently 1 December 2027—that will mean that you will have mobile connectivity outdoors wherever you are in Australia, including the Indi electorate. That will be a game changer for people, because there are areas that currently don't have that coverage. The bill received royal assent yesterday. The next steps will be working through implementation.

In relation to temporary disaster roaming, the three mobile network operators have developed that capability. It has been in effect since 1 October. I'm just looking at my colleague to make sure it hasn't yet been activated, but it is capable, and that will provide another means of connectivity in cases where someone's home network is not available and another operating network can be used. There are some caveats around that, including making sure that it doesn't jeopardise the surviving network, that you still have some connectivity and that people being able to make emergency calls remains a priority. That capability is up and running. I'll just check with Dr Ashurst to see if there's anything that he would like to add.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Before we expand on that, I think it is very important that, whenever we talk about temporary disaster roaming, to be clear that it is separate from the emergency camp-on facility for triple zero calling. Where temporary disaster roaming is activated, one of the considerations that the mobile network operators will be paying very careful attention to is that activating it doesn't put at risk the ability of surviving networks to carry triple zero calls. The emergency camp-on facility operates wherever there is network coverage that would facilitate it, and that's not changed by the availability of temporary disaster roaming. I just think it's important that people understand the two things are separate.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Communications, Media and Sport Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Got it. Does that mean that, for compromised network or patchy compromised network, they will privilege triple zero above other emergency calls? Is that what it means?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Existing requirements on network operators continue to prioritise the carriage of emergency calling traffic. But Dr Ashurst may have something to add on TDR. Thanks for your indulgence.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Communications, Media and Sport Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I've nothing further to add on TDR except to note perhaps that, where it is activated, in order to make sure that the surviving network isn't overwhelmed or over congested, it will be providing voice and text, but there may be some limited data capability, to make sure that surviving network isn't overly congested and continues to function, including to take triple zero calls where required.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Assistant Secretary, Telecommunications Deployment and Preparedness Branch

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is the department communicating this to these regional communities who might be in high-risk areas?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There are a range of different things there. As we said, it's an initiative that is led through the mobile network operators, who are working with their state based contacts. We also work with our colleagues at the National Emergency Management Agency, and when it is a Commonwealth-level emergency, raising TDR as a capability and an issue to see if it is something that is appropriate in those circumstances is something that we are ready for going into the high-risk weather season—or in the high-risk weather season.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's helpful. I want to move on to the ACCC's mobile services inquiry. What has been the impact of this inquiry on regional telco deployment?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's an inquiry that has attracted a lot of interest and enthusiasm, and the focus has been around roaming and roaming more broadly, separate from temporary disaster roaming. The discussion paper has been released, but the inquiry is active and ongoing. The outcomes of it will be considered in the context of the implementation of UOMO, which was a commitment as the legislation went through. Mr Irwin, is there something you wanted to add to that?
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think Ms La Rance covered most of the territory. The ACCC's discussion paper is comprehensive—50 pages and 74 questions they're seeking information on. It covers a range of options. I think the paper is very careful to distinguish between mobile roaming and radio access network, which are different things, and they explain quite well on pages 22 and 23. They have been quite careful to say that their inquiry is not looking at emergency services. That is a separate matter, as we've discussed.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Are the findings of this inquiry going to be implemented as they are handed down, or are we waiting for the inquiry to finish and then for a whole suite of recommendations to be implemented?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The key element in respect of roaming is that ultimately the ACCC will make a decision on whether or not to make a determination for either mobile roaming or radio access network availability. That's a decision of the ACCC. We will obviously be paying very close attention to commentary that the ACCC might provide during the inquiry, but the decision is for the ACCC to make, I assume, at the conclusion of that inquiry.

witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Communications, Media and Sport Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I want to go back to UOMO briefly. Sorry to jump around. Who are the major players in the direct-to-device market currently, and what is the current trajectory of the industry?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The universal outdoor mobile obligation applies to the three mobile network operators—Telstra, Optus and TPG. In terms of the providers of the direct-to-device satellite capability—and I will add that UOMO will be delivered through a combination of existing terrestrial coverage, and, where that is not feasible, then it will be supplemented by direct-to-device capability. Starlink is currently delivering services in Australia for SMS. Voice will be the next iteration of that technology and capability. I think we've given evidence at previous committee hearings that by announcing the intention to deliver direct-to-device services in Australia, and the commitment to UOMO, we have seen more interest in the Australian market. Amazon Leo has announced an intention to develop that direct-to-device capability. AST SpaceMobile and Link are players that we have had conversations with, and that capability is developing. The delivery of those services will be through commercial arrangements with the mobile network operators. That is something that is a matter for the network operators and is still being developed.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you.

What's the department's assessment of the probability that the obligation will actually start on 1 December 2027?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

Can I move to regional connectivity and terrestrial connectivity. I've raised continuing concerns about the savage cuts to regional connectivity programs by the government in the last budget. The 2026-27 budget shows that, while $116 million is being provided under the better connectivity regional program, the funding falls to $32.1 million in 2027-28, $16.8 million in 2028-29 and just $780,000 in 2029-30. How will the government support terrestrial mobile networks in the context of these drastic budget cuts?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I know we discussed these budget figures at budget estimates. There are a range of programs still underway or rolling out as we speak. You'll be aware that we just ran the On Farm Connectivity Program, and we have the upcoming Regional Roads Australia Mobile Program, all under that funding.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry to cut in, but perhaps this is more a matter for the minister, because I'm asking how the government will support terrestrial mobile networks in the context of these savage cuts. This goes to the government's decision to savagely cut regional connectivity programs. Terrestrial networks remain very, very important, Minister, in the regions. How will they be supported by government if all the funding is being cut?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thanks for the question. We are not cutting funding to regional telecommunications. We're actually delivering a billion-dollar better connectivity program, and it includes a thousand projects that are either being delivered or in progress. There's quite a lot in that that's being rolled out. We're delivering 320 new or upgraded mobile cells and towers through the Mobile Black Spot Program. There are the Peri-Urban Mobile Program and the Regional Connectivity Program. We've delivered 600 resilience upgrades like batteries and generators. We've funded a $480 million upgrade to the NBN fixed wireless and satellite technologies and $2.4 billion for the NBN upgrade. And, if you do live in a regional community like mine, you know that the state that the coalition left the NBN in was a really distressing situation for people in regional communities, and that upgrade of 1.5 million premises means that, finally, copper to the future-proof fibre will be completed on time and on budget. We've delivered two rounds of the On Farm Connectivity Program, totalling $30 million in grants, and there's a further round to go. And we've provided $50 million to state and territory governments—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, what I'm asking—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

She's entitled to do that. She hasn't gone overlong in the context of it. Then we'll come back to you, Senator Henderson—actually, we won't come back to you. I'll move the call after this answer.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I have just a couple more things, because it is really important to get this on the record, given the commentary from the senator. We've provided $50 million to state and territory governments to deliver the pilot projects under the Regional Roads Australia Mobile Program. On top of what we've delivered, we are also looking towards what we will deliver in the future, which includes funding for over 100 new and upgraded towers. We've locked in funding for an additional 450 resilience upgrades and, as I said, are delivering the On Farm Connectivity Program for more resilience in communities like the West Coast of Tasmania and the Perth Hills, which I'm sure Senator Smith will ask us about at some stage. Of course, we also recently passed the legislation on the universal outdoor mobile obligation. I would not describe that billion-dollar investment as a 'savage cut to regional communities'.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. I'll move the call to Senator Brown.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I have some questions on digital inclusion for First Nations. Perhaps you could give me an overview of the government's $20 million First Nations Community Wi-Fi Program.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You're talking about the testable community wi-fi solutions we're rolling out to First Nations communities in particular?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Assistant Secretary, Inclusion, News and Media Diversity Branch

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_position: Assistant Secretary, Inclusion, News and Media Diversity Branch

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

text: Finally, on the Australian Digital Inclusion Index, there was an announcement of $6 million that has been provided by the government to help improve data collection. How has that been invested?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Funding for the delivery of that measure was awarded to RMIT University. The grant agreement was executed in late 2024. This has already had some really tremendous results which have been published on our website and on their website.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can you give me an overview.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Certainly. What that funding enabled was for the RMIT to conduct two rounds of data collection through 2024-25 and 2025-26, with a total of up to 5,600 online and face-to-face surveys. In November 2025, they released their first report, Counting on connectivity: measuring digital inclusion for First Nations Australians. That included a First Nations digital inclusion dashboard, which is full of really important insights which will inform not only our program work but also that target 17 refresh you just mentioned. It's a fascinating dashboard with some really sobering numbers in it. Just recently, in May, they released a supplementary report which contains detailed findings of 729 surveys of digital inclusion and communications and media use undertaken by First Nations Australians in 10 specific regional towns. They've gone out and conducted surveys and profiled 10 regional towns and exactly what the digital inclusion experience is.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So is that all the information you have to hand? Otherwise, I will just go and have a look.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's right. That's when the updated reporting will be available, so the fieldwork would be earlier than that.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I will just follow up on one of those questions from Senator Brown. You mentioned wi-fi to WA remote communities—Beagle Bay, among others, Fitzroy Crossing and a few others. How do you measure the impact of provision of wi-fi in terms of improved social outcomes? The absence of wi-fi in some of those communities has been linked to a range of different negative social outcomes or social problems. Is there a way you're able to measure the flow-through benefit of the provision of wi-fi?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As part of the grant agreements, we will be looking at that. Grantees will be required to give us updated reporting as to the level of connectivity and some of the outcomes being achieved. Many of these sites have effectively just gone live, as you've heard, so we will be getting regular reports from grantees to inform us, and we will therefore be able to give more information, as all these sites go live and as they enter that five-year operational period, about some of the benefits that will be achieved. We do hear anecdotally, of course, already that the communities are absolutely noticing the difference, but we'll gather more data on that as the programs carry on.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What program are you funding the wi-fi in WA under?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We were talking about the First Nations Community Wi-Fi program, which was part of the $20 million component of the broader $68 million First Nations digital inclusion package that the government announced a couple of years ago, in the 2024-25 budget.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
Right, so there's $17 million allocated for 2026-27 under the First Nations digital inclusion package. I just want to refer and strongly reject the minister's characterisation of the regional connectivity funding that the government has committed. The departmental question No. SQ 26000582 has just landed this morning. Regrettably, it took over 100 days to get this answer, but the First Nations digital inclusion package is going from $17 million in 2026-27 to zero in 2027-28, 2028-29, 2029-30. The Mobile Black Spot Program is being whittled down to $780,000 in 2029-30. The Mobile Network Hardening Program for 2028-29—zero. There are other programs I won't go through in detail.

The On Farm Connectivity program: only $10 million in 2026-27 and zero in 2027-28, 2028-29 and 2029-30—savage, savage cuts. The Regional Connectivity Program in 2028-29: after $11.4 million in 2027-28, for the following two years there is zero funding. The Regional Roads Australia Mobile Program goes from $11.9 million this financial year to $12 million next financial year to $6 million and then nothing in 2029-30. The Regional Tech Hub, savagely cut, is a service that's doing an incredible job for regional Australians. The Telecommunications Disaster Resilience and Innovation program: $10 million in 2025-26, $3.6 million in 2026-27 and zero in the following three years over the forward estimates.

So, from $114 million allocated in 2025-26 and $116 million in 2026-27, that is dramatically whittled down to $780,000 in 2029-30—less than $1 million for regional connectivity across this country, which I say is an absolute disgrace. And, based on the information that we've just received this morning, I ask the department: have you assessed what the telcos will be contributing to Australia's terrestrial connectivity infrastructure network over the next five years? Because there is literally nothing coming from government by 2029-30. Do you know what the investment pipeline is of the three mobile network operators?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Before the department answers any of the detail on that, I would point out that it is routine for governments to establish programs which are time limited in terms of their funding and then, as budget processes roll around, to have that funding replenished. So, implicit in everything you've just said, there are opportunities for government to extend funding programs or to supplement—
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Betts, this is the forward estimates. This is the decision made by the government—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And funding in the forward estimates is periodically revisited as measures expire and are extended, so we can anticipate future budgets in which some of the programs that you've described are capable of being replenished or extended. But those are decisions for future budgets.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: These are decisions made by this government in the May budget which have shown that a number of these programs have been savagely cut, as I say, from $116 million in 2026-27 to $780,000 only. Are you aware of any other funding that's flowing, Mr Betts?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm just going to respond to that, because it is quite a—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm just asking—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You're making quite a political statement in your question, so if you would let me respond and then—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You've just cut off the secretary. He made a comment.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I haven't cut off the secretary. I'm seeking to respond to your question. I think Mr Betts is fine. The funding in the budget over the forward estimates represents the delivery of an enormous amount of programs, and there are always going to be considerations of future programs in future budgets. It sounds like the proposition you're making is for new projects on top of the thousands that we are delivering to be considered, and we will do that in future budget rounds. But we are not cutting funding. We're actually delivering it.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, that's not what your budget says, Minister.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's what delivery looks like: spending the money that's been allocated and delivering it on the ground.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can I go back to my question, please, Minister?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But if you have a question for the department—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We've got limited time. Is the department aware of the investment pipeline, by interregional connectivity terrestrial networks, over the next five years by the three MNOs?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We do speak regularly with the MNOs about their view of what they will be investing in. Obviously, they're considering a range of things at the moment, including, as you were just discussing, UOMO. I think the strongest evidence will come out of the ACCC inquiry that's underway right now, which certainly will be looking at the investment appetite of the three national mobile network operators. It will be inquiring into that. It's part of the discussion paper they've put out, so we will certainly get more detailed evidence out of that. But we do speak regularly to them, and they are continuing to invest in their networks.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I was asking, specifically, if you are aware of the investment pipeline by the three MNOs into regional connectivity—terrestrial networks, specifically—over the next five years. Do you have that information, or have you sought that information?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As I say, we speak to them regularly. Their plans change all the time depending on investment conditions and depending on their profitability in the market, but we speak to them regularly.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not asking whether you speak to them regularly; I'm asking whether you hold that information or whether you have sought that information.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In relation to the news journalism payments scheme, are you able to outline the support that it provides to smaller publishers and startups?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Certainly. Now that the legislation has passed parliament, we can be very definitive about this. The scheme that's established under the legislation will distribute 90 per cent of the payments that will come into the payment scheme according to a formula that's set out in the legislation. But a further five per cent will be set aside for the Australian Associated Press and a further five per cent for news businesses that are otherwise ineligible. That will often be small publishers, ones that are not yet registered or don't yet have sufficient size to be eligible under the statutory payment scheme. The scheme makes sure that, while there'll be a wide distribution of payments under that 90 per cent amount of funding in the formula-driven payment scheme, there will also be five per cent set aside for other news publishers. I would note that, within that 90 per cent formula-driven approach, there will also be additional weighting allocated to eligible editorial workers in small to medium news corporations, as well as those working in regional and remote areas and those serving diverse communities. There'll be separate uplift within the formula based scheme for those kinds of news publishers and their journalists.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So that final category comes out of the 90 per cent—five per cent to AAP and then five per cent to smaller publishers and startups?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's right.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Australia's traditionally been a pretty tricky environment for smaller publishers and startups to consistently operate in. What are the considerations that informed the five per cent number? And then, perhaps, how are you going to measure its efficacy in terms of the ecosystem?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As we go to establish the details of the payment scheme and the grant schemes that will roll out here, we'll of course build measurement into the funding agreements and the grant agreements that we'll be distributing. I think one of the key points is that, under the statutory payment scheme, there will be a statutory obligation for corporations that receive payments under the scheme to retain the employed journalist in respect of whom they're receiving those payments. We'll of course be required to check that, to make sure that they're acquitting their funding according to the terms of the legislation. I think one of the most important outcomes of this scheme will be to ensure the retention of journalists who are employed with the funding under the scheme—and reporting back to government to ensure that that retention is actually occurring.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Does that extend to a consideration of—let's say, in the small publishers or startups area—retention of journalists but also survival of the institutions, firms and entities in that space?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
Certainly, we know from some of the previous programs we've run that these grants have been absolutely essential to support some of those small publishers. We hear—for example, from organisations like Country Press—how essential the pre-existing grant rounds, like the Journalism Assistance Fund that rolled out previously, have been to support some of those small startups and small regional newspapers that otherwise simply just don't have enough diverse income sources outside of government support. So, yes, we do hear regularly that there are papers that simply would not continue to exist if it weren't for that assistance that's been provided.

The statutory scheme that's been established here will now take on the function that has been previously performed effectively by those grant programs. I would also say that we are rolling out the News Innovation Fund as we speak. Those applications have been assessed for that program, which is designed particularly to support transformation and innovation for some of those publishers to bring themselves into a more competitive state in the digital age. Those grants will be awarded shortly, so there is further support coming even in advance of the statutory scheme, payments for which will commence next year.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: One of the streams you referred to then was those smaller publishers who struggle to generate sufficient revenue on their own, and thus survive, at least in part, due to support. In the startup space, are there examples, or is there a separate category that you identify, where government support has, in effect, allowed a startup in the journalism or news media space to grow and thrive to a point where it needs less support or no government support?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm sure there probably are examples. I don't have them to hand, but we do hear feedback from the sector of how important these grants have been, and we heard very clearly from the sector that the news bargaining incentive legislation was going to be essential to their survival and their ability to adapt in what are clearly very challenging times for public interest journalism.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Challenging, but also quite innovative, I think, and that sort of dovetails into the next question, which relates to the definition of journalism under the news bargaining incentive and the broadening of that definition. Are you able to outline the new aspects of that definition for us and then also what you see the importance of that broadening definition is to the objectives of the incentive?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I know this matter was discussed on the floor of parliament as the bill was going through, and in the end, of course, that broadened definition will allow the scheme to support a broader range of organisations and journalists. In addition to what's in the legislation itself, we will have to develop a series of rules and regulations that will sit under the legislation over the next few months. We've commenced work on that. We will be consulting with the sector on those rules to make absolutely sure we've got them right. We'll seek their views to inform the best possible outcome, to make sure we're supporting the sector in the future.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: This goes back to part of your answer to the first question—what are the supports for smaller communities, businesses and underrepresented communities via the news bargaining incentive?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think the key measure is that additional weighting I mentioned earlier. There's a specific uplift weighting defined in the legislation, as it passed through parliament, that will mean that eligible editorial workers in small to medium corporations but also those in regional and remote areas and those that are dedicated to supporting diverse communities will receive an uplift of an additional weighting through the distribution mechanism. They'll receive a disproportionate amount of the funding as compared to the larger corporations that aren't necessarily serving those diverse communities or those regional and remote communities.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm turning now to the proposed communications legislation amendment bill that was announced by the government in August. There's a provision in that bill relating to the levels of audio description and captioning in free-to-air TV, subscription TV and broadcasting video-on-demand services. Are you able to outline those provisions and the policy goals that they seek to achieve?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. That bill you're referring to that the government announced had five measures in it to support broadcasting, sustainability and accessibility. One of those five measures is indeed the change to audio description captioning requirements. I think my colleague Ms McMullan will be able to take you through the detail of what's proposed there. This is something that we know that the accessibility advocates that we speak to regularly have been asking for, and the government has recognised that in this announcement.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
As part of the broader communications legislation amendment broadcasting sustainability and access bill, there will be an expansion both to audio description and captioning on free-to-air TV and subscriptions. There's been a call for captioning on free-to-air, subscription and broadcasting TV. The details are being settled to some extent, but the situation at the moment is that audio description is available only on ABC and SBS. There's still no audio description on commercial television. The detail of what the minimum required will be—but essentially the legislation will mean that there is a weekly minimum requirement of audio description.

There also is more captioning on TV, but the rules are quite complicated. There are different requirements for free-to-air main channels, for free-to-air multichannels and for streaming versions of channels. Essentially, it's a little unclear and confusing for viewers about when they can expect content to be captioned. The legislation will gradually increase the captioning requirements, including the times and the platforms where captioning will be required, so that the ultimate goal is that people should be able to expect that there will be captioning on TV.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Assistant Secretary, Consumer Safeguards and Regulator Governance Branch

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. I think that will conclude my questioning at this stage. Senator Smith.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Just along some similar themes—is the department working to a timeline, or when does it expect to have some clearer information in regard to which big tech companies will have struck commercial deals with Australian newsrooms and which will have or may have opted for the levy arrangement? You're working to a timeframe?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The timeframes are effectively set out for us in the legislation. Those digital platforms have to do deals by the end of the year if they are to defray their obligations to pay the charge by striking deals. The answer is we are effectively in the deal-making period right now, if you like. We know those conversations are occurring between the digital platforms and news media organisations in Australia. But those conversations are ongoing right now. Deals will be struck. If they are successfully struck, they will be struck by the end of the year and then early in the new year. The ATO in fact will effectively receive the notification about whether people have defrayed their obligations or if they need to pay the charge. I should reassure you that there'll be full transparent information about this made available to the public because the legislation requires that. Once we have information about that and once funding flows in—if it does flow in—to the statutory payment scheme, we will have to publish information about what amounts are available. It will become apparent, and we are required by the legislation to make it public.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Do you have a level of confidence as to what extent big tech might engage—sorry, they are being engaged at the moment, if I hear you correctly. Are you able to give the committee a sense of confidence in terms of to what extent big tech might come to agreements?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can't say so definitively, but we know conversations are happening. We know deals have been struck in the past under the former code. We expect that some deals will be struck. It is probably fair to say that it is likely that not all the platforms will achieve sufficient deals to defray all their obligations. We also expect that some money will be paid as charges into the statutory payment scheme. On exactly what the balance will be of how many deals are struck versus how many end up paying the charge, we're going to have to wait to see how those commercial negotiations go over the next couple of months.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you very much. In this year's budget estimates, the department indicated that it would recommend to government extending the News Media Assistance Program or creating other programs as necessary, based on any evidence that came to the department. Do you have an updated view in regard to that matter?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Referring back to my previous answer, we will have an updated view on that once we have a clearer sense of how much funding has come through in those commercial deals and how much is available under the statutory payment scheme. If some of the larger possible amounts end up in that statutory payment scheme, that'll be a very significant amount of money flowing to the sector under that payment scheme. If, on the other hand, deals are done with a smaller number of media organisations, there may still be gaps that will need to be filled in, and we'll give government advice about that. The answer is that we're monitoring very closely how much money ends up in the statutory payment scheme, and we'll give government advice about whether gaps remain in the sector.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I am particularly interested in the intersection between that awareness of gaps and the diversity measurement review, which I understand is not due until March next year. Is there a risk of a funding shortfall, and how might that be addressed?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: If there is money paid into the scheme, the first payments will have to be made in September next year. That could be a very significant amount of money, but we will know early in the year whether that's the case and we'll be able to provide government advice about that. You're right that the measurement framework will give us further information, but earlier than that we will receive information through the ATO and Treasury about how much money is going to be available in the payment scheme, and that'll allow us to give advice to government.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What's the timeframe around the government delivering on its intention, Minister?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's always a matter for parliament when there's legislation involved. portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

text: Community broadcasting sector concerns aren't a priority for the government?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm talking about the administration of these grant programs.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We've seen the government falter very significantly in relation to another grant program. Have you received any concerns at all in relation to any recipient of any media grant allocated by this department?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I haven't, no.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Has anyone in the department?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

I won't go into the detail now, but there was some concerning material published by this small media organisation. Are you aware of that material at all?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not, no.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Was there any vetting of this grant? Do grant recipients go through a vetting process?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Grant applications are assessed against the guidelines for a grant process; that informs the decision-making to award the grant. As is common across all grant programs, recipients are required by those guidelines to obey all relevant laws and regulations.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Communications, Media and Sport Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can I just ask in more detail about your vetting, please?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Certainly. We can talk about the assessment—
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Before a grant is given to a media organisation, what do you do to make sure that you're not supporting hateful speech, antisemitism or anything else that, frankly, is an affront to social cohesion or to our democratic values?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As Mr Mackay said, the grant guidelines do have a range of eligibility criteria. The criteria that are assessed under that program and under similar programs don't go to us assessing the opinions that have been or will be expressed by the particular media outlet, be it a broadcaster or a publisher, for reasons that I'm sure you would understand. We've designed these programs very carefully to ensure that there's no suggestion that the government is deciding what speech should be funded and what speech shouldn't be funded. So there are no criteria that go to the content of the speech that will be expressed by the fundees. However, as Mr Mackay said, there are absolutely requirements in the grant guidelines and also in any grant agreement that they must abide by all relevant Commonwealth laws and regulations that would apply to any speech.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So, if you had an example where there was a media organisation spreading vile antisemitic sentiments, that's not something that is relevant to your consideration before a grant is awarded?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The test would be whether that constituted illegal racial vilification. We talked about this last time.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So the test is whether it's illegal?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Correct.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So OnePath's grant was discontinued, and the same test was not applied.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We didn't fund OnePath.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Communications, Media and Sport Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, so Home Affairs have discontinued that grant.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's a question for Home Affairs. We don't know the background or history to that.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Your threshold is that, if the speech is unlawful, then the grant either would not proceed or would be withdrawn. Is that right?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, correct. The provisions, as Mr Mackay has explained, relate to either Commonwealth or state law that would enable us to withdraw funding.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Betts, are you concerned about that threshold in light of some of the activities that may be funded under these grant programs?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As we discussed last time, it's for the parliament to determine what is and isn't legal in Australian society, and the parliament considered the enactment of racial vilification laws and vilification laws and considered that it shouldn't proceed. We are working with our colleagues in Home Affairs to look at model clauses in funding agreements to see what scope there may be within that, but we are conscious of the need to strike a balance which doesn't go away between freedom of expression on the one hand and not propagating racial hatred on the other.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can you expand on what you mean by discussing this further with colleagues in the Department of Home Affairs on model clauses.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When we talked at Senate estimates last time, we talked about the dilemma that I've just talked about. We are constantly reviewing the model clauses which go into government funding agreements to see whether there is a way in which we could more explicitly in those funding agreements ensure that recipients, for instance, of grants to support multicultural activities are under a positive obligation to promote those activities and whether there is a way in which we could, without putting our public service decision-makers in an invidious position, find ways of discouraging or prohibiting the use of government grant funding to promote divisive opinions within the community. That is just exploratory work that we're undertaking at the moment. We've been liaising with the special envoy on antisemitism and others, but that is work in progress being led by Home Affairs, and there are complex legal issues of the kind I've described which have yet to be fully resolved.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You raised this last time, particularly in relation to Creative Australia grants, when we were discussing—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, that's correct.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: the concerns about the funding of organisations which were spreading hate, including the Matt Chun essay that I referred to earlier in the day. Since the last estimates—and you did discuss the model clauses specifically in relation to arts funding, but, if you're looking at that more broadly, there hasn't been any progress made since May.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, there has. It's been led by the Department of Home Affairs, who are developing model clauses. That work will be reported into a secretaries' group on social cohesion, of which I'm a part. The model clauses have been under development; that has involved seeking legal advice, including from the Australian Government Solicitor. Decisions on that have yet to be taken, and it may be that we judge that it's appropriate to wait for the findings of the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion before we put substantive decisions to government.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We can take that on notice.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Under the Journalism Assistance Fund, this operates by providing wage subsidies of $39,000 per full-time equivalent journalist over three years. It involves 185 eligible news publishers. Can I ask why News Corporation media outlets are not eligible for that particular grant program?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Are you talking about the Journalism Assistance Fund, which is now a fully assessed and awarded program?
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

text: I raise concerns about this because you've got very long-established in this country—the Geelong Advertiser is in that group and other regional newspapers owned by News Corp are in that group, yet they've all been excluded, yet you're funding the likes of Michael West Media but not the Herald Sun, not the Courier-Mail, not the Geelong Addy, not the Australian. portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As Mr Grunhard said, the decision wasn't made in respect of specific companies, it was a delineation on foreign ownership, which is consistent with a lot of grant programs that the government administers.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That particular position doesn't apply to the news bargaining incentive, as you say; it hasn't applied to many other media programs in the past. Maybe I'll direct this to the minister. Minister, can you explain why your government made a decision to prejudice the newspapers that I've just named?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'll be brief, given the time. That company is foreign owned, so they were excluded from the grant process.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You don't think that the work the Courier-Mail does and the journalists in Brisbane, the work of the Daily Tele nor the work of Geelong Addy are worthy also?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's not about my opinion of certain journalists who work at those organisations. It's about the corporation that runs those organisations, and it is foreign owned. I haven't kept up with the ownership structure, but I think Rupert Murdoch is doing okay for himself at the moment.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
