portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Welcome. Mr Marks, do you wish to make an opening statement?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
Thanks, I will. I appreciate being able to make a brief statement. Before we commence, on behalf of the ABC I would just like to acknowledge Helen Haines. Many others have paid tribute to the role Helen played in this place and in public life generally. But, from an ABC perspective, she's always been a supportive and encouraging person of the work we do. She always makes herself available for interviews, whether in Canberra or in her local electorate office. In fact, she was about to speak to Afternoon Briefing on ABC News Channel that terrible afternoon. She sent a lovely card to the ABC Goulburn Murray team congratulating them for their nomination in the recent Rural Press Club Awards. It reads 'Through bushfires, by-elections and all in between, you have brought thought, care and immense integrity to your reporting while maintaining a strong regional voice. Congratulations and thank you for everything you do.' Of course, the team is devastated by the events of last week. Helen's a strong advocate for her community. In fact, she's been in discussions with the ABC to consider hosting a community event to recognise the tragic bushfires in Victoria earlier this year. I'm pleased to confirm—even though it's not my intent to make announcements in Senate estimates—that our intent is to move forward with a substantial community event in the autumn of 2027 in north-east Victoria, partly thanks to Helen's advocacy. Like everyone's, our hopes and thoughts are with Helen and her family.

In terms of the ABC, there is much to look forward to in 2027. Our content line-up, which was revealed last week—and thank you to Senator Henderson for representing the opposition and joining us on the day—reflects a renewed commitment to distinctive Australian storytelling. With six new scripted dramas, 12 documentaries, a raft of new children's programs, award-winning comedy, everyone's favourite programs and familiar faces returning, there will be something for everyone, whatever their age, interests or background, across screen, news and audio. The line-up reinforces the ABC's position as the home of storytelling, with bold and distinctive content underscoring the ABC's critical role more broadly across the creative industries.

For Australians to have access to their stories—stories that contribute to shaping our nation—the ABC must do more as others, inevitably, do less. Across drama, comedy, children's programs, educational programming, science, arts, religion and history programs, we are doing and need to do more. The ABC is the main supporter of the future of Australian music, and we intend also to do more—all for free, available across the nation and across a range of services. Without the ABC stepping up, access to our Australian stories and our understanding of each other as Australians will suffer. I'm happy to take questions.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, Mr Marks. Senator Henderson.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
Mr Marks and your team, good afternoon. Thank you very much for your attendance. It was my great pleasure to join your presentation of your content line-up and program slate for 2027. I have to say you'll be pleased to know I start this estimates praising some of what looks to be some really exciting programs for next year.

I'll do this carefully, but I just wanted to raise some concerns about the Alan Jones documentary The Rise and Fall of Alan Jones. We saw a trailer of that documentary at a time when Mr Jones is before the courts in relation to allegations. Obviously, that is a matter for the courts. Did you get any legal advice in relation to broadcasting or publishing that trailer? It contains some pretty damning commentary about Mr Jones's character.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure of the exact nature of the legal advice in relation to the trailer that was broadcast during the showcase, but I can assure you that, before the program goes to air, it will be subject to whatever the appropriate rules of the court are and of course appropriate defamatory investigation and advice. We will be ensuring that the program meets all relevant standards and requirements.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is it your intention to broadcast that program prior to the conclusion of the court proceedings?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The exact date of broadcast will be subject to what happens in those proceedings and the timing of those. That's still unknown.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I wasn't raising concerns so much about defamation; it was more about contempt and sub judice.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Did you get any legal advice in relation to playing that trailer?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm sure that would have been subject to advice, but I don't know myself.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Could you take that on notice then?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sure. Absolutely.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I want to firstly start with the concerns about Mahmood Fazal. When you appeared in estimates last time, you said to me, 'Well, he had a great story to tell.' I put it to you that you could have just interviewed him, and it was an egregious error to hire him. Have you reconsidered your position given everything that has unravelled about this particular person?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think my reference to the reasons that they would have had to hire Mr Fazal, and obviously it was before my time at the ABC—we should endeavour to have different voices on the ABC, different voices that come from different backgrounds and communities. That must be one of our objectives. So I always encourage our teams to think differently in the sort of people that they hire. Obviously—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They certainly thought very differently in relation to Mr Fazal. He's not a qualified journalist. He's associated with a crime family. He's got a very dubious background. How did he possibly meet the threshold and standards of the ABC, particularly at a very significant program such as Four Corners?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes; I think they're all fair questions. Obviously, we did a review of Mr Fazal's work and found substantial flaws in much of that work. Mr Fang, in particular, did a lot of detailed background work on that particular issue, and we have taken what I believe now to be the appropriate actions to reflect the failures in Mr Fazal's work at the ABC.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Where did things go so dramatically wrong?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: If you are asking me, it does feel like Mr Fazal was given perhaps not sufficient management and supervision in the exercise of his stories. Obviously, we've also made some quite significant changes to the editorial team for Four Corners as well. So I think it's an area that we've looked at quite broadly, and I think we feel that we're in the right direction now with really strong new editorial leadership. Obviously, there's already a great team of reporters there, so we're feeling very confident about the future. I don't know if you want to add anything to that, Mr Fang?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The only thing I'd add is that, as the MD said, we've taken action against the stories which we didn't think met our standards, and we've looked at those standards. We're also going through a process of having a look at our guidance, particularly around the use of anonymous sources and how we review that and who needs to know about who the people are and the verification that we need to do. There are different approaches in journalism around anonymous sources, at times, and it has been convention that not all sources are necessarily named to program EPs and others, but we think that we need to be clearer for our teams about what we expect there.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Marks, can I just put to you that this is not just a matter of supervision. Mr Fazal wasn't even qualified—didn't even have the appropriate qualifications—to serve as a pre-eminent, long-form current affairs journalist at Four Corners, and yet he was hired. When complaints were made, a number of years ago—and I know you weren't there as managing director; this was before your time—the ABC covered that up and instead put out a glowing statement saying how much the program and the ABC supported Mr Fazal. These concerns included threats to others, in writing.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We have obviously looked in detail at all of that, since my arrival at the ABC. I think we can take confidence that there are many great people who do work for Four Corners and, with new editorial leadership, we are obviously very confident as to its future. Obviously, there were mistakes made. We've taken action to rectify those and take the steps that we think are necessary to put Four Corners in the best possible position to do the best work it can. We don't resile from the decisions that were made. They were important decisions. The points you make are valid ones. I think we've proven that we've taken the steps that are necessary.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Fang, were you involved in this matter at the time?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You're the editorial director of the ABC—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That wasn't my role at the time.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What was your role at the time?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I was in news, and I was either working—overseeing our national and international services. I wasn't connected to our current affairs programs.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Marks, have you made any changes at the ABC in light of the fiasco involving Mr Fazal?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Obviously, we've had a change in the Director of News. We obviously have had a change in the Executive Producer of Four Corners. I think the deputy of Four Corners has also left the program, and the program reported to the head of investigations. I can't remember the exact time—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is that Ms Puccini? She's now gone.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: She has also left the organisation. So we have made substantial changes. Investigative journalism is a really fundamental body of work, and it's so important to the future of our democracy. We have to get it right. It has to be done at the highest standards. I think we've taken a number of decisions and put people into important positions that I think will reflect the body of work going forward.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What about the training and minimum standards of training that are expected at the ABC? I've continuously raised concerns about the very disparate requirements when it comes to journalistic standards and training. Have you changed your requirements in that respect?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, it's an important area that Mr Fang leads. I'll let Mr Fang respond.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We're following up specifically on the reports of the ombudsman about this matter and about some of the work I just mentioned before about anonymous sources and our guidance, and we'll do specific training around that. We continue to do broad editorial policy training across all of our staff. I think we've spoken about that before. We just ran a week of intensive training, looking at a variety of different editorial policy issues. We have just rolled out and piloted a new training module, designed for investigations and investigative leads, for editorial leaders to focus more clearly on the responsibilities and editorial issues that come up there.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What about the qualifications of journalists you hire? What's the minimum standard, because Mr Fazal did not have any formal journalistic qualifications?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What we try to do at the ABC, and in the media more generally, is access the skills and experiences of a broad range of people in the community.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can you address that question, though? What are the minimum journalistic qualifications required to be a journalist at the ABC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When you say qualifications, what do you mean?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What are the minimum qualifications?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: To start with, every person that joins the ABC in a journalistic role needs to complete basic editorial policy training. Many people come through a cadetship process or through other processes. They're generally put into roles that are junior in nature, and they're mentored by senior staff.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When they apply for a job, what are the minimum requirements or qualifications for the role? Are they meant to have gone through a cadetship program if they're a graduate? If university qualifications are not required, is there any other tertiary qualification that is required? What are the minimum qualifications for journalists when they are hired at the ABC? I say this because I believe that, certainly through your TikTok journalism, there are a number of so-called journalists who have got no formal journalistic training at all. Do you have minimum journalistic requirements insofar as the qualifications that are required before you are eligible to join the ABC as a journalist?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Firstly, I don't think there's any difference between journalists and those who work for content makers that are making content for social media platforms. I wouldn't suggest that they are any less qualified just because they're junior—some of them are junior.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm asking you, what are the minimum qualifications? I've raised concerns—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We do not have a minimum university qualification. We look to engage with people—many of them do have qualifications, which might be in journalism or different fields. For other people, if they bring a level of experience or if they bring other skills, it's possible that we could bring them in and train them onsite.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Do you have any way of benchmarking whether someone would be appropriate and suitable to be a journalist at the ABC? If they're not required to have university qualifications, are they required to have work experience? Are they required to have formal cadetship training? Are they required to have worked in an equivalent field? Are you saying to me that you don't have any minimum threshold as to standards?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I'm saying applying for these roles is competitive, and we would of course weigh up people's levels of experience as they relate to the media. If we were looking to bring in somebody that had limited media experience, we would absolutely expect that they would have some experience in writing or in some of those fields, or maybe they would bring in some other skill set. We don't have a list of standardised qualifications that we expect every journalist to bring to a hiring process.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: On a related matter, Mr Marks, how many journalists and others do you employ in the news and current affairs division of the ABC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Ms Amorelli might have that data.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There are about 2,000 staff in the news division.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: On notice, could you please give me a breakdown for each of those persons at the ABC—unidentified of course—of where they're located in the country; the role they perform; their title, to the extent that it's describing the nature of their work; and their qualifications.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. I think what we could do is look at some broad groupings of roles across the organisation—how many are journalists and how many researchers or other professionals. Obviously you're seeing the rise of video journalists as an important category at the moment. We can look at where those are broken down across the country. I'm sure we can provide that level of information.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: How many are in Sydney? What's the breakdown of the roles? How many are in Perth, Renmark, Geelong—wherever it might be. Could we get a very detailed breakdown of those 2,000 ABC journalists, producers, editors and other staff in news and current affairs—I realise there are a lot of people—by where they are located, how they are qualified and the work that they are doing.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Just to give you an idea, Senator, I think somewhere around 700 to 800 of those people are located in regional and rural offices, but I don't know whether they're of the journalistic number. Let us come back with some information and see what we can provide to you.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you very much. I'd be very keen to look at that detailed breakdown, please. I want to go to the issue of the reports of a number of journalists working in the Middle East who subsequently were discovered to be operatives of or associated with Hamas. Are you familiar with that issue, Mr Marks?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, I don't know about 'a number of journalists', Senator. I think there was a cameraman, wasn't it, Mr Fang, or—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: A fixer—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: a fixer who I think did some work for the ABC. You probably know the detail better than I do, Mr Fang.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Whatever the question is, I'm happy to answer it.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: My question is: could you please give us information about this matter, including whether the ABC has hired anyone who has subsequently been identified as being someone who is a member or operative of Hamas or associated with Hamas?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think you're referring to a story that was pinpointing some work that had been done by the Committee to Protect Journalists. It's an international organisation, very well respected, who maintains a list of journalists that have been killed in conflicts around the world, including in the Middle East. There was one particular item which made an allegation about a fixer that used to work for the ABC—I'd have to get you the exact year, but it was some years ago—who was killed in Gaza. The Committee to Protect Journalists has not removed that person from their list of journalists that have been killed, so their view is that person was a legitimate journalist. We have attempted to get some clarification from the IDF about their position on this. As yet, they have not provided us with any evidence to suggest otherwise. So, to the best of our knowledge, for the work that we have done and that the Committee to Protect Journalists has done, that person was a legitimate journalist that was tragically killed.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What evidence do you have to support that, given this person was on an IDF list of people associated with Hamas?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't think it's incumbent on us to prove a negative in that sense. The internationally recognised list that many media organisations refer to around this maintains a high level of credibility around this matter and still continues to list that person as a journalist. We have asked for further evidence from the IDF, and, until we are able to find something that goes to the veracity of that claim, I don't think it's incumbent on us to make a decision to declare that that person was a member of Hamas.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's incumbent on you to ensure that you're not hiring journalists who work for a terrorist organisation, Mr Fang. This person has been identified as a fighter in the Hamas military wing—Mr Roshdi Sarraj. Have you investigated that at all?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As I said, Senator, that's not the information that we have been able to ascertain. Until we hear otherwise, he remains a person listed as a journalist. We, of course, do due diligence around who we work with. The person you're referring to had worked with a number of different media organisations. To the best of our knowledge, he was a legitimate journalist and fixer—and he was killed.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm going to raise serious concerns about this. This person has been identified as a fighter in the Hamas military wing. I appreciate that you didn't know that at the time, and I appreciate that this person is deceased. Have you ascertained whether you have hired or utilised any other journalist in your coverage in the Middle East who is connected with Hamas?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, you're providing information that I do not have. We have not been given evidence to suggest that that person who was killed was a member of the Hamas military wing. There have been claims made, but we have to operate on a higher evidentiary basis than that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
There's been a number of significant reports about this. My question is: have you investigated this matter? I refer to an article in the Australian, ''ABC's man in Hamas' exposed as being part of IDF's list of terrorists'. I'm reading the first paragraph:

A Gaza-based "journalist" who freelanced for the ABC and was remembered in Australia as an "amazing professional" is among 170 media workers killed in Gaza since October 7, 2023, who have been accused of being Hamas terrorists after an extensive Israeli Defence Forces investigation.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As I said, we have asked the IDF to provide us with evidence of that matter, and we have not been provided with evidence to assure us that—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's what I was asking about, if you'd investigated that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Absolutely, yes. We have asked.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Good, that's what I was asking. You have actually sought that information.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Absolutely.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What were the nature of your discussions with the IDF in relation to this particular individual?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I haven't done that directly. I understand that our international team have done that, but they have gone seeking to find out the nature of the claims around this particular person because it's important for us to know the veracity of that allegation. We have not been provided with any evidence of that at this time.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, Senator Henderson, I'll come back to you—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can I ask for that correspondence on notice and any other inquiries you've made in relation to this. I'll be very quick—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You can ask for that on notice, but I need to move the call. I'll come back to you. Senator Thorpe.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: If it's going to be about Islamophobia, then I'll leave the room while that conversation happens because it's actually disgustingly violent as well. Mr Marks, in your opening statement, you mentioned about all Australians having access to their stories—stories that contribute to shaping our nation. The ABC must do more as others inevitably do less. Without the ABC stepping up, access to our Australian stories and our understanding of each other as Australians will suffer. Let's talk about Tony Armstrong and Always Was Tonight. The ABC made one episode which attracted strong criticism from right-wing media commentators and conservative politicians. They went right off; the truth was hitting them hard. Was the program developed as a pilot for a potential series, or was it commissioned from the outset as just a one-off special?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's a good question. I can't talk to the motivations, but my understanding was that it was a one-off. It was obviously considered for recommission, but my view was that it was going to be hard to replicate the success of the first program. We are doing more episodes of another show, called That Blackfella Show, as an alternative to doing multiple one-offs. That's the direction we've gone in, and that show was also a great success and something that, next year, we're going to do a series of as opposed to a one-off.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Were you, Mr Marks, involved in any conversations about the program's future before the decision was made not to proceed with further episodes, and did you discuss or raise the right-wing criticism with anyone inside the ABC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't think it was about criticism. It was a question of whether that show could continue to maintain the standards that it set in the first episode. Many things we do here will get reactions from various sections of society, and, in general terms, I think the act even contemplates that we'll do things that will be controversial from time to time. The question for me is: what is repeatable and what are we able to build a reputation around? Yes, I sit in the commission meetings for those programs, and the decision has been made to go in a different direction and extend the run of something else. It's not a criticism of the program or its elements, and it's not a reaction to the controversial nature of claims that were made against it. It's just what we feel is the most repeatable formats for the benefits of as broad an audience as possible.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand it would be unusual for the ABC MD to intervene directly, but in this case did you make a captains call?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No. I think that was the decision of the commissioning committee, and of course not everyone is going to agree with that decision, but I think, for the ABC, it's the right way to go forward.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Are you aware of staff at any point being told that there would be a longer series? That's what I've heard.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm sure that would have been the hope. It's the hope of every creative with their programs, but I wasn't ever fully aware—I think even the proposal to bring it back was as another one off. I don't think it was proposed to come back as a series. I could be wrong. I wasn't aware of the staff being told it would be a series.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Soon after the decision not to proceed with further episodes of Always Was Tonight, the ABC quietly abolished the role of Head of Indigenous TV. Under this role there were shows like Message Stick, Black Comedy, Redfern Now, and Total Control. Who made the decision to abolish the position, and did you approve it personally?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We were endeavouring to elevate the position of First Nations content within the organisation to a direct report to myself. At the moment, we have a First Nations strategy role. I'd like that First Nations strategy to move on to be a general content role in the organisation and, as I said, to be present at the most senior levels of the organisation. It is a really important category of storytelling that the ABC needs to do a substantial body of work on. We take that responsibility very seriously. We're now in a consultation process with our First Nations staff about how best to set that up for the future, and I suspect the person that occupies that role going forward will then be able to ensure that whatever we do is amplified and extended not just on screen but across our audio and news divisions as well. What I want to do is when we do something is do it really well and get more out of it. Elevating a role, I guess, was my hope. The changes that we proposed did not land well with the staff. We've paused them, and we're now going through a broader consultation period process. I'm sitting in those meetings myself. I sat in them with about 12 First Nations staff the other day. It was a really productive discussion, and I expect we'll end up with a commissioner who will operate at the most senior level of the organisation.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand there was a change document that was produced in relation to some of these decisions. Are you able to provide that on notice?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's what I was just discussing. There was a change proposal, which was to make the First Nations division of the ABC an all platform or all genre division, rather than having it siloed in each of the individual news, audio and screen divisions. I don't think we communicated the proposal well. It certainly didn't land well with staff. It caused a lot of angst. That's why we paused the proposal and, as I said, I'm participating in a broader discussion with our First Nations staff. It's quite complex to get to a landing on what is the right structure for us to be able to tell those stories as well as we possibly can going forward, but we've got a broad cross-section of First Nations staff involved in that process. I think they all feel well heard, so I'm sure we'll come out with a really positive outcome by the end of that. It might take a few months, but we'll get there. If your question is 'are these stories important to be told?'—they are. It's important that the ABC tells them. It's an important part of the statement that I made earlier today. It's actually an important thing for me personally to make sure that we do that in the best possible way. But I want those programs to be great reflections of the contribution that First Nations culture makes to our broader culture. I think we're on the right path, but we've got some work to do to get there.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You promised to be more open, as the ABC's leader, yet the removal of the head of Indigenous TV role was never publicly announced or explained, and only limited staff within the ABC knew of it. Why didn't you tell the public that ABC was removing a longstanding, dedicated Indigenous leadership position?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure that it was a secret decision. Ms Amorelli might have something to add about this. Obviously, we were respectful of that person and not wanting to make it look like it was something to do with his performance. So we were certainly respectful and not looking to make a lot of noise about it, but I don't think it was a secret decision at any stage. And it did go to wide consultation.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It wasn't intended at all to be a decision made in secret or not communicated more widely. If that's how it's landed, it wasn't intended that way. Subsequent to that, the change proposal that's been discussed was communicated, and we've made decisions about that, which Mr Marks has just described.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Why was the head of Indigenous TV position abolished before meaningful consultation with First Nations staff had taken place? Will you reinstate that position if that's what your First Nations staff want?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think yes, we'll go through that consultation process. It's an interesting challenge that we have as to who gets to make the decisions about what content happens and why and where the agency sits for that sort of decision-making. As I said at the beginning of this discussion, I want that to sit at the most senior levels of the organisation. I would imagine that the head of First Nations inside the ABC will have content responsibilities going forward and will have authority to make more decisions about the sort of content that we do. In the scripted area, in particular, we are recruiting for an executive who is capable of ensuring appropriate cultural implementation of any stories that we're doing in addition to being actively involved in the First Nations programs that we do. There are a number of First Nations programs that we are in production on at the moment, so ensuring that we've got the most senior level of script executive—we do have a First Nations consultant, but we need to make sure that we have an executive responsible, creatively, for those shows, as well. It's something we're looking to recruit for.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The government hasn't cut any ABC funding, yet you've been running redundancies. How many positions have been made redundant since you became managing director? Is that figure more than 100?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I would say so.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can talk to the FY 2026 financial year. There were 76 redundancies actioned. To date this financial year, there have been 18 redundancies in total. We currently do have a workplace change proposal out at the moment about our screen operations division that's still in play. Consultation just closed on Friday. But that's the total number—76 for last financial year and 18 to date this year.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: How many were First Nations?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't have that number. I'd have to take that on notice.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Please. I'm not sure how much time I've got.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'll move the call in one moment, so if you've got one more question—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There's been no proposal to reduce our First Nations staff that I'm aware of. I think even in the change proposal it was mooted in the area. I don't think there was a loss of roles. I think it was the same number of roles. But my job, partly, is—and this is something that I'm quite passionate about—as I would call it, to get more money on screen to deliver more content and services to audiences. If there are areas within the ABC that need to change to enable us to do that, I think we need to be prepared to continue to make those decisions, but, as I said, I'm not sure—there's certainly not any proposal to reduce our First Nations staff or content.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. I will put the rest on notice.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Whitten.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I previously asked about a breakdown of your expenditure between radio, TV and online content. At the last estimates, you provided me with an excerpt from the 2025 annual report, with some commentary around the line items, but there's no commentary around the two biggest line items: employee benefits and suppliers. Is there no segment reporting at the ABC that allocates cost between the three distinct platforms?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Increasingly it's becoming blurred. As you would appreciate, audiences are less concerned about whether something originated from the audio screen or news department. They're just consuming the content, and increasingly that content is across all platforms. It is getting more difficult to be able to distinguish between the three areas. In fact, I think it'll be something where we will rally around categories of content going forward. Sport, First Nations, specialist content, Australian music—this will be the way that we will set up for the future. News has traditionally been the largest component of content spend at the ABC. I don't anticipate reducing the budget of the news division. I think there are many areas of news that could do with a lot more money. And then screen and audio would come in that order. That would be the traditional way that we would look at it, but, going forward, I think you'll find it'll become a lot more blurred and we'll start to talk about genres of content rather than platforms.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So there's no way of distinguishing between the allocation of funds—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Increasingly that's going to be more difficult. In terms of the way that we budget, there would certainly be, if you were interested, some general breakdowns that we could provide you which would reflect the budget in the way that, historically, the organisation has approached budgeted cost across the three areas.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
It would be of interest.

In the June 2026 Stuff the British Stole episode 'Flag Fall', students at Perth Modern School were asked to redesign the Australian flag. Every featured design removed the Union Jack and emphasised multicultural, inclusive or Indigenous elements. Students stated the current flag does not feel distinctly Australian or representative of modern Australia, with nothing to the contrary. What editorial process determined which student views and designs were included or excluded?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's an independently produced program, so that would have been something done—I think that program is made by a business based in Canberra. It would have been subject to editorial review within the organisation. The editorial review would have been 'Does it comply with our editorial policies?' Again, that's an area that Mr Fang heads up. I would say in response that it's a relevant perspective. Were a broad section of students involved in that program? I can't answer that question, unfortunately, as it would be an independently produced show. I don't know if there's anything that's come across your desk on that one, Mr Fang.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No. Unfortunately, I haven't seen that episode of Stuff the British Stole.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Your editorial policy, like you just said, requires presentation of a diversity of perspectives so that no significant strand of thought within the community is knowingly excluded. Now, given the Institute of Public Affairs poll from 25 May found that 72 per cent of 18- to 24-year-olds wanted to retain the current flag, it appears the program has actually pushed a false consensus that is apart from the reality of how young people and young Australians feel about the flag. Are you concerned that your programming is influencing young people to reject our national symbols by creating a false consensus?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I would be concerned about anything that pushed a false position. I think it sounds like they were responding to a challenge that was provided to redesign the flag, so I wouldn't take that as something that was a proposal or something that was being pushed by the ABC. I hear your concerns. I would want to ensure that a range of perspectives would have been considered from students in that program. Again, unfortunately, I haven't seen it, but your point is that all perspectives should be considered, and I would have imagined that that would be the case. Maybe the challenge should not have been to redesign the flag but to keep or redesign. Maybe that would have been a better challenge.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: For balance, would you consider a program called Stuff the British Gave Us?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It'd be an interesting program! Are you into pitching, Senator?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I'm not. But that would be a balance of perspectives under your rules.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I was just going to add for your further information that one of the members of my team has indicated that they did look at that program. The program was looking more broadly at the history of the Union Jack, so it was looking into that. In particular, there was the genesis of the English flag and whether actually it was linked to a flag from the Republic of Genoa back in 1190. So it was a historical look at the English flag, and that one particular segment, in my understanding, was really just a scene to get children to think about the broader story of the history of the Union Jack and its origins.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I just have an issue with encourage our encouraging our children to think about a new flag, given that brave men and women put it on their shoulder and go to war for us.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand, but I don't think that the ABC could be accused of not running across the year a variety of other programming and material that looks at the contributions of Australians in different ways. You specifically spoke about one particular instance. We cover extensively, for example, Anzac Day and the parades and marches around that. We run a whole series of programming on Australia Day, Australia Day marches, citizenship ceremonies and a variety of other programming. If you look across the balance of our output, I think we can stand by that we are providing a good cross-section of the relevant history of Australia.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Keep up the balance. Thank you.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. When you approached the commissioner, did you provide a list of questions in advance, and did those contain a reference to One Nation cartoons?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't know that. I'd have to take that on notice.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. The host asked the commissioner—I don't watch much TV at all, come to think of it, not just the ABC, so I don't know the host at the moment.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So you haven't seen the program that we're talking about?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I have seen it but not the commissioner. I've seen snippets of it. The host asked the commissioner—is that David Speers?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The host asked the commissioner about causes of political violence. One Nation cartoons were mentioned obliquely with the words 'a cartoon that suggests someone should be hit by a car'. The commissioner picked her words carefully—and that's not a criticism—and avoided direct criticism of One Nation's cartoons. Has the ABC stated in any editorial in any medium that the commissioner stated that One Nation cartoons were causing violence?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I wouldn't believe so. I watched that interview. I thought it was a really interesting interview. As you said, the commissioner picked her words very carefully and was very specific about what she was endeavouring to say. I thought it was a really balanced and interesting interview that led to some good discussion on the couch afterwards about the issues. I don't think there was a particular focus on a One Nation cartoon in a way that might have indicated something that—I'm not entirely sure what you're suggesting, I'm afraid.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, if you watched it, did the commissioner make a connection—make the link—between One Nation cartoons and violence?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can't remember exactly what the commissioner said entirely, but if you wanted to have a better understanding of what occurred, you need to watch the full interview.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm concerned about media reports of the interview, which were wrong, and I wondered if you'd join that club.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Oh, I see. I haven't seen other media reporting that would have picked up on that particular issue that you're suggesting in my reading.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Could you check, for your own benefit, within the ABC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Within the ABC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sure. We can check that. Have you seen an article, Senator, which you're suggesting—you might be able to help me out here by pointing me in the direction of the one you've seen.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't check the ABC for every medium, but I noted other media have portrayed that—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Right.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: so I'd like to make sure that you know what the ABC is doing.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Okay, I'll attempt to check something there.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I want to pick up on the concerns I've raised about the ABC hiring journalists who were subsequently found to be Hamas operatives. On 24 September, the Washington Post reported that a rights group said that some people classified as journalists killed in Gaza were militants. The Committee to Protect Journalists says that 19 Palestinians killed by Israeli fire who it had previously identified as journalists or media workers were actually militants or participants in combat. Are you aware of the Committee to Protect Journalists' concerns in that regard?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Absolutely—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Marks?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, Senator, I think Mr Fang was referring to that earlier.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Absolutely, Senator. In fact, we have updated a number of ABC stories to reflect those updated numbers.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Oh, right. Well, thank you for that helpful additional information, because you have published a number of stories, and I've just had a look, and one story is still online speaking very favourably about one of these journalists who is actually on the list of 170 journalists now identified as Hamas operatives. That story is still live.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You'd have to let me know which particular story that is, Senator, and we'll have a look at it.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: 'Journalists in Gaza are writing their own obituaries, after Israel brands them "terrorists"'—posted on 12 August 2025. That is still live, and it speaks in quite glowing terms about Mr Anas al-Sharif—I'll table this document—and he is one of the identified journalists by the IDF.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thanks, Senator. But you're not suggesting that person worked for the ABC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No; I'm just saying that you've said you've corrected a number of your publications. This particular publication is still speaking about this Hamas operative in very glowing terms.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm happy to have a look at that, and, if that's incorrect, we'll fix it.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So how thorough was your review of your work if I can find within minutes an article praising this person, Mr al-Sharif, who was identified as a Hamas operative?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

text: Absolutely I can. Those would be mentioned, I would imagine, on our web page where we note corrections and clarifications—if it was a correction. So I'd have to have a look at that. But I can certainly see what we can provide.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'll get you an exact number.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Do you know the number?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't know what the number of articles is, no.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When I raised questions with you earlier, you said that you had not taken, from what I recall, any particular action, because you had not received any evidence in relation to the fact that the journalist who worked for you was a Hamas terrorist.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think that—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, Senator, could you repeat that last part of the question?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In relation to the journalist working for the ABC, what action have you taken to remove that person's work?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Are you talking about the person that—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think the senator is referring to the stringer that we were talking about earlier. That person still exists, as I understand it from Mr Fang, on the list of journalists that were killed in Gaza.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Correct.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We have responded, as Mr Fang earlier said, by seeking to do our own inquiries of the IDF as to whether that person is a person of concern from the IDF's perspective or not. We have not received a response, to this date. So, at this point, that journalist, based on the evidence we currently have, remains someone that was tragically killed in Gaza. The fact that they've been listed in other sources as being a Hamas operative, as you suggest, is one perspective. I think we are basing our work on that international body's work and direct questions to the IDF, which are the appropriate steps to take.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Marks, I'm getting very confusing evidence here. You've just told me: 'That's just one perspective. We don't know. We can't verify.' Yet, in relation to the 170 journalists on this list, Mr Fang has just told me and this committee that you've removed a range of stories in relation to these journalists.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, I might have been misinterpreted. We have taken action around the change in the list that the committee for the protection of journalists made. They removed 19 people from their list, and those are the things that we have corrected. I think what you're talking about is a separate claim from the IDF about a number of other people. The committee for the protection of journalists has acted on 19 names, not on the other names that the IDF may or may not have indicated.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In relation to the three that I have named—and I'll table this—Mr Sarraj, al-Sharif and Karim Shabat, you have published articles praising, at the very least, one of those persons. I've just cited that particular article.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: For clarity, which list are those three people on?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They're on the IDF list. Anas al-Sharif has been identified as a Hamas operative. There's an article that you have published, which is still online, speaking about him in very favourable terms. Have you reviewed the articles which praise journalists that have subsequently found to be Hamas terrorists?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, you're using the terminology that they have been 'found to be' Hamas terrorists. We're relying on and we are working on the evidentiary standard that the committee for the protection of journalists provides and our own work which we can attribute towards these people. The fact that the IDF has made a claim about a number of other people does not necessarily mean that we have yet been able to, or have, verified that those people are Hamas terrorists. So you are referencing the IDF list, and I'm speaking about the committee for the protection of journalists.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So you're not believing the IDF. Is that what we can take out of this?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, what I'm saying—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The IDF has conducted investigations over many, many months. This has been published recently, but this is the result of very extensive work done by one of our closest allies. They have produced this list, and are you saying that you are not going to take this list seriously?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I'm not saying that at all. I'm not making a claim about the IDF in any way. I'm saying that, as you would expect, we would take an independent lens to verification and to ensuring that the people that we have worked with are not on some of those lists. It's about the level of verification that we want to do to check in these things.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You said before that you've contacted or written to the IDF. Have you?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'd have to check on the way that the contact was made. I know we have spoken to the IDF and have received some feedback from them, but we have not been provided with anything from them that to date is evidence of the claim that the fixer that we worked with was a member of Hamas. We still remain utilising the committee for the protection of journalists list.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Fang, in relation to this stringer that you hired, the IDF has their Hamas ID card. The fact that you're not regarding seriously this work is deeply concerning. On this list of 170 journalists, have you checked whether you have hired any other journalist at all on this list?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'd have to take on notice and let you know what we can provide on the other names, but, as to the work that's been done around that particular person, as I've said, we haven't seen any evidence as yet provided that would move us to make that classification.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's outrageous, Mr Fang. It's right here. This is the work of the defence force of one of our closest allies—of Israel. Their work includes the fact that Mr Sarraj has a Hamas ID card, and you don't think that's sufficient evidence.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, we need—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You're just being completely disregarding of the fact that the ABC, prima facie, based on this evidence, has been hiring Hamas terrorists. Now, I'm not saying you were aware of that at the time, but, now that you are aware of it, my concern is that you are completely disregarding this evidence.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I don't think that's what we're doing, Senator. We have asked to find out more information, and, as yet, we haven't been provided with information that allows us to make that determination.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Marks, I would say to you that Mr Fang is being completely flippant in relation to this matter. There's very, very serious and significant evidence in relation to the ABC stringer—that he was someone the ABC hired who was a Hamas terrorist—and the fact that you are being so flippant about the very significant evidence uncovered by the IDF is deeply concerning, Mr Fang.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm really shocked by this.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't think Mr Fang is being flippant at all, Senator. I think he's taking the matter very seriously. Again, as he said, we have written—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, he hasn't, Mr Marks. He has said—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Chair—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: He has basically said—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Chair, do you think that they could answer, maybe?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: that he doesn't find the evidence compelling enough.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, did you want to raise a point of order?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I just was wondering if the witnesses could finish their answers before being interrupted again. It might help.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I didn't necessarily think that Mr Marks was continuing an answer. But, if you were, Mr Marks—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: He was trying.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: would you like to finish it, then, and I'll come back to Senator Henderson?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think the categorisation of Mr Fang as flippant is incorrect. I think he takes it very seriously, and we are looking to ensure that we have verifiable information that we believe we can act on. Now, obviously allegations have been made, and that has caused us to make inquiry. When we get the result of that inquiry, then we will be prepared to take action. I think that's actually taking it very seriously rather than flippantly, Senator.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can you provide on notice the names of all journalists and media companies in Gaza who the ABC has hired, going back to 1 January 2023?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, Senator. All journalists—and what was the other part?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Media companies in Gaza the ABC has hired—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sure. I'm sure that we can—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: because some of these journalists work for other media organisations. They may have been used by the ABC. I assume you haven't done that investigation.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is your question: can we cross-check all of the names that have been notified by the IDF as being Hamas operatives as to whether any of those people were employed by the ABC? If that's the question, then that's certainly something we can provide.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That was my earlier question, but I would like it if you could provide that on notice. You haven't done that cross-checking?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No other thing has come to our attention—that I'm aware of—that would cause us concern other than the particular stringer that you mentioned.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Fang, when I said 'you haven't done that cross-checking', you shook your head, so the answer is no?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, it's not. It's that I'd need to go away and check and let you know.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So have you done that cross-checking?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I personally have not done that work. I'd have to check what else was done, but also, if you wouldn't mind, we have not been provided with any Hamas identity card either, so it would be great if you could provide that to us, if that's—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Fang, I'm telling you that the IDF has said that it has, as part of its work, uncovered Hamas ID cards. I do not have the Hamas ID cards, but what I'm saying is that the evidence is overwhelming and very compelling, and yet you've indicated to me that that is not sufficient other than that you've made some inquiries of the IDF.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm sorry. I thought you just said that you were showing a Hamas ID card for the particular person in question that worked for the ABC.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I said that the IDF had located the fact that they had Hamas ID cards.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Anyway, I think the correct step here for us to take is—we are treating the matter seriously. We have asked the IDF for confirmation as to the evidence they have. Based on the response that we get from the IDF, we will take the appropriate action. I think we treat it very seriously, and that is the appropriate action at this point in time, and those are the steps that Mr Fang has outlined.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Marks, I'm not convinced that you have treated this seriously, because I can't get an answer as to whether you've appropriately cross-checked the list of 170 journalists on this list. There's no sense at all that the ABC has undertaken appropriate due diligence, and, despite the evidence that's been uncovered, you've confirmed today that you haven't taken any action in relation to this ABC stringer who you hired a number of years ago.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't agree. I think we have taken action, and we've also acted based on the work of—I can never remember the committee.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Committee for the protection of journalists.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Committee for the protection of journalists—and have taken appropriate action with the other story, so I don't accept your assertion that we've taken no action. I think we have acted.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I didn't say you'd taken no action. I just said I don't—I am incredulous that you haven't taken this more seriously and the evidence that's been uncovered.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson, I need to share the call. Thank you. I have some questions about ABC and the copyright protection of its material. Does the ABC monitor the use of ABC content by third parties?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It can be difficult, obviously, to do. There is a particularly more difficult environment when it goes to social media. There are tools that we can use, particularly with YouTube, to register IP as owned by the ABC, and YouTube and Google will act on that to ensure that breaches are notified to us. Other environments are more difficult for us to be able to get that information. In mainstream media, when we're made aware of things, then, obviously, we can take action, but there's no automatic notification telling us that IP has been infringed.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And so you would register major ABC IP with YouTube, perhaps flagship shows, perhaps iconic shows that the ABC has, like Bluey?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Bluey would be a bit of a different example. We don't own the IP. That's owned by an independent producer based in Queensland, so that would be their step to take that action rather than ours in that particular case.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Does the ABC have processes or procedures to protect its own copyright once that use is discovered?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, if it's an ABC copyright, then we will consider whether there has been an infringement and take action. On the case of ABC licensed copyright, such as that in Bluey, that is something for which we would have to work in conjunction with the IP owner to take that action.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In a political cartoon released by Pauline Hanson's One Nation party on or around 18 October 2024—it was called 'The state of Melbourne'; I've seen it on YouTube—the cartoon character Bluey is depicted, identified by name, shown driving an SUV then running over former premier Daniel Andrews, reversing over him a number of times. Did the ABC have discussions about licensing that content to Pauline Hanson's One Nation party?
