portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Not that I'm aware of.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Were you aware of this cartoon?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Only recently has it come to my attention.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And you don't know whether the ABC was involved in discussions about licensing it?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The ABC would not have been involved in that discussion.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Did Pauline Hanson's One Nation party seek your permission to use that content in that way?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Did Pauline Hanson's One Nation pay you or the independent licence holder for the use of Bluey's likeness in that content?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Certainly not the ABC and, I would assume, not the independent production company or BBC Studios—who, as we all know, unfortunately is the distributor of that content. In that case, either the BBC or the independent producer should have consulted the ABC before any such licence of copyright would have occurred. So I think I can assume that no such discussion happened.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So you have a right to be consulted in that context because it's licensed content?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Correct.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In light of that, what is the ABC doing about this?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The first step is to consider whether there is a legal right for that character to be used in that way. I struggle to ascertain whether there would be a legal right, from my legal background. One could only assume that there would be some fair dealing, which might be satire or parody—might be. But it's not a parody of any Bluey work. It's not a minor use of the IP. In my view, it is an infringement of the intellectual property—No.1. But it's also a shocking use of Australia's most loved character—in fact, probably the globally most loved character—in a video that is both shocking and disrespectful to the children of Australia, who love that character so much. So I can't substantiate it either legally or on the basis of its usage.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Using a children's character to run over a political figure with a car—I appreciate it was published two years ago, but it's had a particular poignance in the last week. Have you sought legal advice in relation to this matter?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We have. In fact, I was in discussion with my general counsel about this the other day who was telling me that they were considering whether there was any basis on which that could be implied as fair use. My opinion was I would find it very difficult to believe that there was any fair usage base for that IP.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Have you contacted the Queensland licence holder?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That discussion has also happened.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Have you contacted BBC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure of that, but I'm sure that process will have happened as well.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: How did you contact the licence holder?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It would have been in discussions between our head of commissioning and Ludo films, but I'm more than happy to come back to you with progress on that matter, because I think it's a blatant use of IP.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, I would like you to come back to me on that. I'm not asking for anything that's privileged or within the content of legal advice, but I would like any file notes or memos that don't fall within legal professional privilege to be provided on notice along with any correspondence, with the licence holder in Queensland and in relation to the BBC. Have you contacted the One Nation party about this use?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The first thing would be to make sure that we're confident of the nature of the action that we would take, before writing a letter to seek its removal.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Putting it at a different level, rather than a pure assertion of legal right, given what I think is a pretty heinous use of Bluey in that cartoon, have you contacted the One Nation political party to express the view you expressed to me just a moment ago?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I only became aware of this last week. Again, I've left it with my general counsel for the week, but we will be taking further action, I can assure you.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: At this point, what further action is in your contemplation?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I would imagine that it's a breach of intellectual property, and a cease-and-desist letter should be issued.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is there any further action that you're considering?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I guess, in intellectual property claims, there sometimes is a right to damages, but I think in this case damages are going to be an insufficient remedy. So something in the nature of injunctive relief, ultimately, would be what you would seek.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Why do you say damages are going to be an insufficient remedy?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't imagine that, necessarily, it would be difficult to prove the damage that the copyright holder or the ABC has suffered in this particular case, and I would say that that damage is not—again, I'm testing my legal background here—a sufficient remedy in this particular case. The remedy should be stop.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Bluey is a pretty valuable product, though, to the licence holder and with its licence rights to the ABC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, Senator. It is a very valuable product.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Do you think its association with the ABC is valuable to the ABC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Definitely.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Okay then, can I ask you to reflect on that answer in terms of damages and whether there has been a loss in the depiction in this way?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Certainly, Senator. We'll take all relevant advice and take the appropriate steps.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: If you could keep me updated on this, that would be fantastic.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Will do.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. Senator Roberts.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
On 12 July this year, your show Race Around the World aired a four-minute animation, a cartoon titled A Very Relaxing Video, which included a graphic fantasy of assaulting Gina Rinehart and turning her body into a sausage roll. After more than 1,000 complaints, the ABC pulled the show, removed the offending cartoon and published an apology from the author, which you endorsed. In part, it said:

The sense of humour featured … is farcical. In no way was it my intention to promote violence. My writing is cartoonish and always satirical.

So it's okay for you to produce a violent satirical cartoon and only pull it after legal threats from Gina Rinehart? You actually said cartoons are satire, yet still used your Insiders show to try and denigrate One Nation cartoons for doing the same thing last week. On this matter, was the ABC being hypocritical or dishonest or politically biased?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No. With that particular program you refer to, we received complaints about the program. We went through a complaint process to understand whether the program was in breach of guidelines or not. The Ombudsman found that it was not in breach of our guidelines, but I made the decision, subsequent to that, that the guidelines didn't sufficiently reflect community standards on the issue. We've changed our community standards as a result. It's a matter we take very seriously and we took appropriate action.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In September this year, ABC News released a three minute magazine video titled Let's Talk About Kink, which was most positive about kinks including furries, sex workers, BDSM and a constructive discussion around consenting to safe choking. This is the second time the ABC has spent taxpayers' money on this topic. Yumi Stynes did an episode of ABC podcast Ladies, We Need to Talk in 2023 on the same subject. Are you using your budget for what matters to you, not taxpayers?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not aware of the particular program that you refer to. If you're happy to provide us with the details, we will have a look at how it meets our editorial standards.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I want to raise a couple of additional concerns in relation to the Hamas terrorists and the links with the ABC. You mentioned that you had asked your international staff to contact the IDF. Is that correct?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Are they journalists working full-time for the ABC?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You haven't engaged any third party to contact the IDF?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Not that I'm aware of, Senator.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Who is doing that work?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I would have to come back to you with a specific name. It's part of our international team. That's what I'm aware of.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Based in—?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In Sydney.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Oh, based in Sydney?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I believe so, but I'd have to go back and give you the exact detail of how that approach was made.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What is the ABC doing to vet journalists and media companies in Gaza to make sure that you are not hiring terrorists?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Most of our journalism comes from ABC employees—longstanding employees—for the journalism part. On occasion we will hire stringers. These are often people that facilitate our access to or use of facilities in these places. They're not necessarily providing journalism or influencing editorial. So I think you can rest assured that the vast majority of editorial material that we provide is from longstanding and proven ABC verified journalists. The role of stringer is somewhat different to the role of journalist in this particular case.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sure, but, given what has happened, what steps are you taking, if any, to vet journalists and media companies to ensure that you are not hiring Hamas terrorists?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As I said, the great bulk of ABC journalism that we do is by people that have been vetted through our process and, obviously, built up reputation over time. On occasion it is difficult in a location—as you would appreciate, Gaza would have been so at the time; sometimes Iran can be. We don't have a lot of access to those places, so on those occasions sometimes we will reach out to stringers or third-party companies to seek to get access or footage or whatever it might be. We go through a vigorous process to ensure that we vet everything that is delivered to the ABC. Obviously, there is an allegation in this particular case that a stringer or a fixer—again, which is someone that's helping us on ground rather than doing journalism—is involved in Hamas. We are, as Mr Fang said, taking very seriously the nature of that allegation and seeking to verify it ourselves. But I think you can take confidence that our journalism is influenced by longstanding ABC employees.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In relation to the Hamas ID numbers linked to the ABC stringer, they have been published on the IDF's website. They are actually publicly available.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm sure the IDF will respond to our inquiries, and, again, we will assess and take appropriate action, as will, I imagine the Committee to Protect Journalists.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When did you make those inquiries, can I ask?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't have the exact date in front of me. It was in the past couple of weeks, when the CPJ made changes to its list.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Have you interrogated the CPJ's list?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: My understanding is we've spoken to them and had a conversation with them about the way that they do their work to try to make sure that we're comfortable with that. I don't have information about whether we've gone name by name, if that is what you're asking.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There are 19 people that have been identified as being Hamas terrorists on their list. Have you double-checked or cross-checked that list?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In what way?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: To ensure that you haven't directly or indirectly hired one of those people on that list.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'd have to take that on notice and see exactly what we've done.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. I would like to also ask some questions about Mrs Rinehart and the inclusion of that disgusting segment in the Race Around the World program. On what basis was that satire, Mr Marks? I have to say, of all the comments I've heard out of the ABC, I thought it was quite nonsensical and improbable to suggest that that was satire and that's why it was justified to include it in the program. How can that possibly be defended as satire?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It was certainly the intent for it to be satire from the young journalist who created the film. On whether satire lands or not, often it doesn't; sometimes it does. Again, we went through an editorial review process and complaints process. That complaints process came to an outcome and we made decisions that I felt were important to set as the standard for ABC work going forward. We acknowledged the error, we apologised for the offence and we've taken the appropriate steps.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It took you quite a few weeks, though, to apologise, and in fact the ABC itself defended this as satire.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Every person in Australia is entitled to go through the same complaints process in relation to content that the ABC broadcasts. There will on occasion be things that I might look at, mainly news content, for accuracy or impartiality reasons where I might say, 'That doesn't meet standards,' and act faster, but generally, for the validity of our complaints process, it's important that I let it run its course so that we know the basis on which we're making decisions. In that case, we had to let it run its course, and I acted straightaway on the release of that decision by the ombudsman. So I don't think there was a delay.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'd put it to you that it was not appropriate for you not to immediately apologise. It was very self-evident that that was completely unacceptable material to be publishing and distributing in the way that the ABC did. Why didn't you apologise straightaway?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As I said, every Australian is entitled to go through the same complaints process and it's important that I myself don't prejudge that process with statements. It's important that we go through to complete that process so we understand the nature of the decision that we're making.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But, Mr Marks—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Otherwise, we've got chaos.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: that was a farce. The ombudsman found there was no breach of editorial policies. That was a farce.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And, as a result, my decision was that our editorial processes, policies and guidelines didn't sufficiently deal with the depictions of violence directed towards individuals. We've made a decision that we're going to update our guidance. I'm not sure whether we've—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's okay. Yes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We've now completed that process. We took the appropriate steps: we apologised and made the changes necessary to the film to ensure that the harm didn't continue.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What steps were taken? In relation to content that may cause harm or offence, that needs to be referred to senior editorial staff under your editorial policies. Did that occur in relation to this program?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In this case the matter was not referred up. It certainly wasn't referred to me or my direct report—in this case, the head of screen. So that upward referral didn't happen. That's also a matter that we have sought—sorry, we have ensured that there's clarification going forward that any matter like that potential controversy should be subject to more senior editorial review.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Smith, you've got a couple of questions.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I want to go back to an earlier remark. Mr Marks, given everything that has happened in this country in recent times, you said that the ABC's editorial guidelines were improved following this episode and the depiction concerning Mrs Rinehart. It took this incident, as gross—my word—as it was, to require or lead to an upgrade in the editorial guidelines specifically in regard to violence. Given everything that has happened in this country and globally in recent times—I'm glad it did take an event to upgrade the guidelines, but I'm surprised that an episode on 12 July triggered that, given everything that has happened in this country. Has the ABC been asleep?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, Senator. I think it's a really interesting question—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
No, it's more than interesting. Mr Marks, I've got to be very, very serious with you. I am a person who has refrained from a lot of commentary about the ABC but has sat at these estimates for a number of years now. In your opening remarks, you said:

In terms of the ABC, there is much to look forward to in 2027 … six new scripted dramas, 12 documentaries, a raft of new children's programs, award-winning comedy, everyone's favourite programs and familiar faces returning, there will be something for everyone, whatever their age, interests or background …

But the airing of that segment on 12 July has undone whatever goodwill there might have been left in this country for the ABC. It's like one step forward and then a hundred steps backwards. My question is: why hadn't the editorial guidelines been upgraded in regard to violence long before this particular matter, given everything that has happened in this country in recent times?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I guess my statement about interest was an explanation as to the guidelines. I'll let Mr Fang talk about this in a minute. Too often our guidelines are determined by reference to news and current affairs standards, and this program was not a news and current affairs program. It was an entertainment program.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Poor entertainment.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The news and current affairs exemptions or guidelines require us, as you would appreciate, to sometimes display violence that occurs in a news context and to be able to find a circumstance in which to do that within the guidelines. Obviously the guidelines as drafted, probably overthinking about the news and current affairs context, didn't necessarily distinguish what might happen in an entertainment program, so that was an error. It took this process to really understand that something that had been contemplated for a news context didn't work in an entertainment context. Do you want to add anything to that, Mr Fang?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: To build out on that, the harm and offence guidance has always recognised issues around violence; it's not that it hasn't, and, as the MD says, primarily that has been around measuring or weighing up whether depictions of violence are justified in a news context against the public interest that's required to show that. What we've attempted to do with the update to the guidance is to make it even more specifically clear in non-news content—it was already a consideration—to be more specific about some of the expectations of the community and to make it clearer to our content makers, when they're making non-news content, the considerations to make when weighing up purpose against potential harm and the standards that the community has. We're trying to make that guidance even clearer so that where these questions—which are matters of judgement, often—and these matters of judgement come up, we are crystal clear about the expectations around our editorial guidance when it comes to harm and offence, particularly around non-news material.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That might be an explanation, but I find it completely unsatisfactory. The ABC operates in a very dynamic context, the living world, and to think that its responsiveness is restricted to a complaints mechanism—to public outcry, disappointment, outrage—is just not good enough. That's just not good enough in this day and age, particularly given more recent events that we've been witness to. That's just not good enough. Mr Fang, you talk about a matter of judgement, but I thought, Mr Marks, you were inferring that, in terms of the editorial guidelines that were followed, these decisions were made at a junior level—my word, not your word—of the organisation. If judgement is required in applying editorial policies and guidelines, why is that judgement exercised at such a junior level of the organisation and not a more senior level, particularly in matters concerning violence?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes; we've also made steps to ensure that not only matters that might meet the guidelines but also matters of taste are referred up to more senior people in the organisation. Those are steps that we've taken.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In earlier inquiry today, I asked the minister when and how did Minister Wells convey her views about the unacceptability of this particular episode to the ABC. Did she convey them to you, Mr Marks?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Not to me personally, Senator, but obviously we were fully aware of the minister's public statements and communications happened privately between members of my team and the minister's office in relation to this matter. We were under no illusion as to the minister's view in relation to this content.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That is not the same as the minister conveying her view to the ABC. The distinct impression I got from you, Senator Green—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I took on notice to get you the details of how that was expressed.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The distinct impression I got from you—no, you took on notice 'how'.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I took on notice the details, because I didn't have them this morning.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The distinct impression I got from you was that Minister Wells had personally conveyed her view that this was unacceptable. It was a conversation between ABC staff and the minister 's staff?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Again, Senator, I'm not aware of exactly the details. It didn't come to me personally. It went into the ABC in different angles. I think the minister's saying she's undertaken to come back with details about the exact nature of those communications. But, as I said, from the public statements made by the minister, it was clear as to the minister's views in relation to this content.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. I'm going to go to our break now.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We'll resume with the ABC. Who am I handing the call to—the coalition? Senator Smith.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Continuing with the episode of Race Around the World on 12 July, I have a number of specific questions to ask and then others I'll put on notice. It's my understanding that under section 8 of the ABC Act, the board has a statutory duty to ensure the ABC's functions are performed efficiently and with maximum benefit to the Australian people and to maintain the integrity of the corporation. What governance questions did the board consider were raised by the approval and broadcast of the sexually violent material referring to Mrs Rinehart, broadcast on Race Around the World on 12 July 2026?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
I think the board wanted to understand exactly the matters that are being discussed here today. On what basis was the material able to go to air, what was the decision-making process that facilitated that and, in response to, obviously, the clear community standards that had been contravened, what actions were we going to take? I think the board understood my insistence that a complaints process should proceed and that we shouldn't prejudge the complaints process and that we would be prepared to make the decision as soon as that process was completed.

I certainly accept that there are matters of taste that are also independent of matters of guidelines, but the guidelines are the basis on which the ABC does operate. So it was an important part of the process to go through that process and then look at what we needed to change at the back of that. Mr Fang has been responsible for those changes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What date was the board meeting at which the matter was first raised and considered?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'd have to come back to you on that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Actually, what was the date of the first board meeting and dates of any subsequent formal or informal board meetings where the matter was raised? Were board papers prepared?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Editorial complaints process matters are subject to a document that goes to board. So it would have been part of that process, but I'm not sure of the exact dates or whether there was a board meeting between when the matter happened and when we'd taken the appropriate steps. I'd have to come back to you on that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, please. If there were no board meeting, what is the mechanism by which you would discuss this with the board?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Generally that would be through the chair, and the chair would talk to me as the managing director to get an understanding of basically the things that I've outlined just previously. It's certainly something on which the chair will have a view, and he'll express his view to me, and we will agree on a course of action that I am following, whether that's the appropriate course of action or not.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So if there was a formal board meeting and there were board papers prepared, could you make them available to the committee? Was ABC management requested to provide the board with an explanation of how the material had been approved, separate from the complaints documentation that flows to the board in the normal way?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure of the exact paper, but I would have updated the board in my managing director's report as to what happened and why. That, often, is not subject to a formal board process but a verbal update from me at board meetings.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Just to be clear—we did canvass this before the break—did you or any member of the ABC board discuss the segment with the Minister for Communications or her office at any stage, or with any other member of the government, before it was broadcast?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Before it was broadcast? Not that I know. I doubt that would have happened, but I can talk only from my own perspective.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Did you discuss it with the minister or her office at any stage following the broadcast, and on what instances was it discussed between you or others at the ABC and the minister or her staff?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I didn't discuss it with the minister directly. Minister Green has offered to come back with details about the nature of the communications that happened if it was to happen, or when that happened. That's to come back to committee.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The Prime Minister also made some comments later in August—perhaps even a week after the minister's comment. On notice, could you advise whether you or staff at the ABC spoke with the Prime Minister or the Prime Minister's office in regard to this matter?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can't take that on notice, because that would be a matter for PM&C, but if the ABC is willing to do that?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Again, I did not, but we can undertake to come back to you as to whether the Prime Minister's office communicated with the ABC.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What other instances can you recall of content depicting, describing or condoning physical violence against a named, living Australian woman the ABC has approved or broadcast?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's a very difficult question for me to answer—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'd hope the answer was 'none'.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not aware of any. Mr Fang, are you aware of any?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We have much comedy; I'm sure there are many instances of matters where prominent Australians have been subject to comedy on the ABC. Whether it's in the nature of violence or not, I can't respond.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The Ombudsman acknowledged that violent language directed at a named public figure may have greater impact because violence against women is a significant concern. What consideration did the ABC give to that issue before broadcast, rather than after complaints were received?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As I've mentioned, the program was referred to editorial policies for guidance as to whether it met the editorial guidelines or not, so it wasn't a matter that was taken lightly. It was a matter that was subject that was subject to appropriate review. As I said, the wrong decisions were made, but it was subject to review within the organisation before broadcast.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: How can taxpayers have confidence in the ABC's existing editorial controls when material which the managing director subsequently says should not have aired nevertheless passed the production, editorial, compliance and classification processes?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We have put in place clearer guidelines to ensure that not only matters that may be in breach of editorial guidelines but also matters that may be controversial or considered to be in bad taste are upward-referred. Will everything come through that process? I hope so. Might there be errors that are still made? It's possible. A lot of content is made across the organisation every day, in various forms, and it's impossible for me, or anyone, to stay across that as an individual, but I think we can take confidence that through the changes we've made to both the upward referral process and the guidelines we are far better placed than when this matter occurred.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Just to be clear, what were the editorial layers that were observed in this particular matter—not those that weren't observed, those that were observed? My understanding is that the editorial policies require content that 'may cause harm or offence' to be referred to senior editorial staff. Can you detail for me what the layers were and then whether they were at a suitably senior level to fulfil the editorial policy requirements.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: My understanding is that the program was referred up to the executive producer of the program—or the person that was in charge; it may be another title—in the screen division and that there was discussion and advice sought about the segment. That's a senior role, and ordinarily that level of seniority would be sufficient to sign off on a program. If at that point the judgement call had been made that it should have been referred up, it should have then gone higher, but it wasn't in this case.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There aren't Chinese walls operating in the ABC, are there? What I mean by that is people, when sending something up the editorial line, sending it just so far and then consciously not sending it further up the line because they have a level of awareness or understanding that there might be some pushback. It's gone to the executive producer, and at that level just discussion and advice was sought, and what you're saying, Mr Fang, is that at that point the judgement decision that was made has subsequently been determined to be wrong, the wrong judgement.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, Senator.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So why, at that level, would it stop—a matter depicting violence?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What the policies really look to do is to refer up when a matter is contentious. It's a judgement call. Most of the time there would be a discussion in a general sense about all programs. In this particular matter I said it was the executive producer but I think it was referred up to what we call 'head level'. That's a very high level. Apologies if I gave the wrong designation before. We seek to have accountability, I suppose, at the right level around programs. If at that point it wasn't determined that it needed to go further, it wouldn't have. At that point, though, if advice is sought and someone says, 'I think you need to refer that up,' or if it is a contentious matter, for example, often, particularly in the news context, it's an advisory to the manager that goes higher—up to the director of news, for instance—so that they are aware and can intervene if they like. In this scenario, my understanding is that it would not be unusual, it would be common practice, for a program of this nature to go to head level. It would not always go to the director of the screen division. But, under the changes that we've made to our guidance, it's more likely that that would have been a refer-up decision.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: On notice, can you give me, in detail, the decision-making process that was applied in this particular matter—job titles and, if appropriate, individuals—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, we'll see what we can provide.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
and then a clear understanding of the decision-making that was undertaken in this context and the decision-making layers that sit above that but were not utilised in this particular context.

When was the last time the editorial policies of the ABC were externally reviewed?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They're publicly available, so in a sense—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's not the same as being—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: we're always having a review.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's publicly scrutinised. That's not the same as publicly reviewed.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure when the last time was that there was a full external review. I'd have to find out about that. But, obviously, as you have indicated, these are and need to be living documents, and we are on continuous review around our guidance and policies.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I'm not so sure that is true, given the evidence of Mr Marks. There have been a lot of incidents of violence in this country. It took this particular episode on 12 July for there to be a review. Mr Marks, that is something that I'm asking you to consciously think about and also to convey to the board. I might choose to write to the board independently of that. When was the last time the complaints process at the ABC was independently reviewed? I'm thinking from the Australian National Audit Office perspective.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. The creation of the ombudsman, which is now 3½ years old, I believe, was the result of an independent review of the complaints process. I was going to add that, as part of that review, there was obviously an examination of or a look at the editorial policies and how they apply, and there were some eminent Australians who were involved in having a look at that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I recall that now that you say it, yes. Thanks very much. Thanks for your cooperation.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I want to pick up on a couple of additional questions in relation to the Race Around The World program. Mr Marks, as you know, I was concerned that, from day one, you didn't make the judgement that this was inappropriate and that an immediate apology was warranted. As the editor-in-chief, I think that would have been appropriate. But what also concerned me was that on 25 July the ABC published a statement defending this what can only be called sexually violent segment as 'editorially justifiable'. Did you approve that statement prior to publication?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think the statement that you're referring to was made by the particular contestant. Is that the statement that you're referring to?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No. It's the ABC's statement.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, I would have approved that statement, and it would have related to the intent of what the piece was. It was always intended to be a piece of satire, not taken seriously. Obviously, we also have a duty of care, which is very important to participants in our programs. So, taking all those factors into account, it was important to outline why the program could have gone to air, and the basis on which it did was satire.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think, Mr Marks, you'd have to agree now that that's just nonsense. It was not editorially justifiable, and I think you made a serious error in approving that statement and in not apologising straightaway, which was all that Mrs Rinehart was seeking. Do you concede that you have erred and that you should have responded much more immediately with an apology and a decision in relation to this program?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's a very dangerous step, Senator, if I am intervening in the case of every piece of content to express my view about whether it meets guidelines or is warranted or is not. I think it is important that we have a complaints process, it is important that everybody goes through that same process, and that's what happened on this particular occasion. I just think the alternative is very difficult for me to manage personally and is not the right policy for the organisation. We have to go through the formal complaints process. It has to apply equally to every piece of content and every person.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Marks, that doesn't make any sense, because you did intervene. The ABC issued a statement saying it was 'editorially justifiable'. It didn't say, 'Look, this matter is under investigation.' A judgement call was made, and I'm putting to you that that was an intervention, and it was the wrong judgement call.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand your position. I think it was important for us to be able to outline early in the piece what the intent of that particular segment was—obviously, to inform the audience. In the end, community standards—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What do you mean by intent to inform the audience?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The intent of the piece was a piece of satire. That was the editorial justification for it to go to air.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But that's a nonsense. There was nothing funny or remotely comedic about this. It was gross and disgusting.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand that. In the end, that was the decision that was made—that it wasn't justifiable.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Who made the decision to broadcast this program? This didn't go live to air. This went through an extensive approvals process. There was a panel involved as well. Who approved the program for broadcast?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, I think Mr Fang has just outlined in response to Senator Smith that we will answer on notice the detail around which the process happened and what steps didn't happen. We will come back on that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But I would like to know specifically who approved the program, Mr Marks.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, I think Mr Fang has undertaken to respond on that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Do you know who approved the program? Was it the EP? Was it the supervising producer?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, I think Mr Fang has already responded that the EP was involved and then the head of entertainment would have been involved as the head of the relevant division.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Did they ring any alarm bells at all?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They went through a process, obviously, of legal advice and editorial advice. That process came back with decisions that it was not in breach of the guidelines. We've explained the reasons why the guidelines—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There was an earlier process whereby the EP and the person that he or she reports to was involved in determining it was not a breach of the guidelines? So that is prior to that going to the ombudsman?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Correct. That's before broadcast. Obviously in the context of the broadcast as well, one of the judges, Leigh Sales, was able to express her distaste of the segment. So the program in the whole context was provided, including Ms Sales's rejection of the program as being editorially justified. There are a bunch of things here. In the end, the view was the guidelines didn't appropriately deal with the issue, and we made the decisions accordingly.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Have you apologised personally to Mrs Rinehart?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I tried to contact Ms Rinehart, but she would not make herself available.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Did you write to her expressing or conveying an apology?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I thought the public apology was the correct step to take.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So no private correspondence at all?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I have not been asked for a private apology. I think the public apology was generally in these matters the appropriate step to take. Private apologies are a lesser standard, I would argue.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Could you provide on notice the correspondence and the internal communications—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We'll come back with the material that Senator Smith asked for.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: that were had in relation prior to that ombudsman decision being made, including all the internal correspondence, please, Mr Marks?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. We will come back. I think what was asked was: what was the process; how was it followed; what decisions were made; and what steps in that process weren't followed or weren't elevated? We'll come back with that information.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Could you also please add to the list the internal correspondence in relation to the vetting and the approval?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We'll see what we can provide on that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Did you have any communications at all with the ombudsman in relation to these complaints?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As in?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Did you or anyone in your team have any correspondence or communications?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No. It's important when an ombudsman's process starts that the ombudsman is independent of the organisation. They need to conduct their work independently of management.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, the ombudsman is an employee of the ABC.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sure, but we respect the independence of that role. I think that is a very important part of the way the organisation works.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I did an interview on ABC Radio National a number of weeks ago. I was asked about Mr Fazal and was critical in relation to that appointment. To be fair, a lot of ABC journalists are horrified about the decision that was made and the failure of the ABC to act when complaints were first made. I also cited a number of other concerns in relation to the ABC's impartiality and standards. I was critical for a few seconds of Sarah Ferguson in relation to her conflict of interest involving the documentary of which she is the EP funded primarily by Animals Australia. That conflict of interest was not declared at the time she became the EP, as we now know. That part of the transcript was removed from the ABC's website. The ABC subsequently released a statement saying it was removed on legal advice. What legal advice was provided that led to that part of the interview being removed?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm happy to help on that one. Just to be clear—I know you know this—there was an interview on Radio National. It went live to air. Subsequently, as is pretty common practice, we turn around material to replay. My understanding is that the program, which it always does, sought some legal advice. They were given advice that there might have been an issue with a particular part of that item. They clipped it up. It's not unusual for them to do that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What time did they seek legal advice?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't know what the exact time was. It was clearly after the live radio interview had gone to air.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Because the interview was at 10 to seven in the morning, approximately. That section of the transcript was removed pretty quickly afterwards. When I checked it, my recollection was it was gone by about half past eight.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It doesn't surprise me. We have to serve markets in different times across the country.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What was the illegal issue in me raising conflict of interest concerns about Sarah Ferguson?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not a lawyer. I would have to rely on ABC Legal's view on that. They made a recommendation that piece of content should be removed.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So they made that, what, at 7.30 in the morning or a quarter to eight?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't know the exact time, but they made it prior to the next deadline for that program to go up on repeat.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Who gave that legal advice?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't know the specific name of the lawyer. We have lawyers on standby routinely.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Fang, can I tell you that there was no legal issue with me raising concerns about Ms Ferguson at all. It wasn't defamatory. What I said was true. It was probably one sentence or two. There were other criticisms that I made which had far stronger language in relation to Mr Fazal. It's just not credible to suggest that was removed because of legal advice. I find it very difficult to believe. I think it was removed because there were obviously sensitivities in me criticising another host of ABC current affairs on an ABC current affairs radio program.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Again, the interview went to air live. You were able to make your statement. Whether or not I agree with the decision I haven't said. There was clearly legal advice which they acted on.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: This was just an attempt to cover it up. When I found this out, I was walking back with a coffee in Parliament House. I ran into a couple of ABC personnel. I told them what happened. It was clear that the ABC felt uncomfortable that I had criticised one of your fellow journalists. I understand being uncomfortable, but it looks to me like you've concocted a story about legal advice to justify removing that part of the interview that I had with Sally Sara.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand, Senator. I'm telling you what happened. What the perception might have been is totally up to you, but I'm telling you what occurred.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Not even your own people believe this, Mr Fang. What evidence can you provide me that legal advice was sought? Who sought the advice?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I am happy to provide on notice what we can to demonstrate to you what occurred.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Was it the EP of Radio National?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I believe it was the program team as they would routinely do. Again, I am happy to provide what we have to assure you of the process that happened here.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Marks, it really does not look good. I'm sorry.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm sorry, but—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The fact is that was removed. If the ABC wanted to remove it because it didn't like it, just say so. But the fact that the ABC, I believe, is concocting a reason based on legal advice to remove that is just silly.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, I reject that there is any concoction going on. What happened is—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, what happened is what Mr Fang said. It happens routinely. All the programs before they go up online are subject to review. These things happen very quickly given the volume. That's what happened. There was no great conspiracy, concoction or expression of a view from anyone on high saying, 'Please delete that from the article online.' It didn't happen. It was a legal process.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: My concern is that the ABC hasn't told the truth. I understand why there is sensitivity. I don't take issue with that. What I'm concerned about is that someone has not been candid with the facts. If there were a legal problem with what I said, what is it? You are a former lawyer. Could you tell me the legal issue with what I said?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I imagine—again, I'm not aware of the legal advice—there would be concerns about defamation. As a result they would have taken action. As Mr Fang has said, we'll come back to you with the details. I can assure you, based on my understanding, that there is no great conspiracy.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't have a lot of confidence in the ABC's ability to manage defamation cases. Look what happened with Heston Russell. As you well know, Mr Marks, truth is an absolute defence in defamation. I said nothing other than a factual statement.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, I'm not aware of the statement that was made so it's difficult for me to respond to that. My understanding is what Mr Fang has outlined is what happened. This is the side of it. We are not sensitive to comments made by our people. We all live in a world where we are subject to scrutiny, as we should be. So that is not what went on here. There was a legal review. The legal review came to that outcome. It's as simple as that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There was a legal review between 7 am and 8.30 am, was there?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Our lawyers are available 24/7 for legal review. They have to be, given the nature of the organisation. I'm not sure exactly what the process is for that uploading of the digital article. Before it is uploaded, it would have gone to an editorial review.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It happens every day.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I haven't received a legal letter from you, Mr Marks.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, it's not something—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: If this is an issue of defamation, I would have thought the ABC would follow through and I would get a concerns notice.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It obviously doesn't reach that threshold.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, yes. In fact, it was a very spurious claim. There was no proper basis to it. There has been no proper legal claim. The ABC has not raised any concerns with me that what I said was defamatory. I just have real issues with the fact that the ABC has, I think, concocted a reason to remove that part of the interview in the transcript.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I reject the assertion, as I've said. Mr Fang will come back with the details of what occurred.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can provide the documentation that outlines what happened, Senator.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. If you could provide all of the internal documentation—the messages, who gave the advice, what the advice was.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think I can provide, Senator, what you need to know to reassure yourself of the fact that this is not what happened.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I just want the ABC to be honest. That's my concern.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, I am sitting here. I'm telling you what happened.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I would like all of the documentation, please, in relation to this matter held by the ABC.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We can absolutely provide all of it.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So all of the messages or the correspondence, the notes between all personnel in relation to the legal advice and the decision made to remove that part of the transcript. The ABC has every right when politicians remove bits of transcripts. It just doesn't look good. No-one would have even said a thing about this, Mr Marks, but here we are discussing Ms Ferguson in Senate estimates again. I'm not suggesting that I know; there is no evidence that she intervened in any way. It does not pass the smell test, if I can say it that way.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I understand your assertions, but I reject them. I think Mr Fang has outlined what happened in this case. It's a fast paced thing. I'm not sure there are going to be extensive documents with legal advice and the like. It's a decision made.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Oh, great.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, it's in the moment. It's a decision made on the run. We will come back, as Mr Fang said, with the details of what happened as much as we can. I'm sure you will be satisfied that there is no greater purpose or higher order intervening in this matter.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure that I will be satisfied, Mr Marks.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We need to move to the next outcome.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There are other matters. Just quickly, there was a termination payment made to Mr Stevens which has been published in your annual report. Could you just explain the basis of it? portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sure, Senator. As you would imagine, following Mr Stevens's resignation, we have the option to ask Mr Stevens to continue to work through his notice period or for me to ask him not to work out his notice period. I felt it was important given what had happened that I ask him not to work out his notice period and to pay him his contractual entitlement to do so. That is what occurred.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That was the contractual entitlement for the duration of his fixed term contract?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There or thereabouts. I think the payment reflected what his notice period was. Obviously, I felt it was important that we move forward with new leadership, so I didn't want to continue Mr Stevens in that role.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That is a little different to the way you characterised it the last time we spoke.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Not at all. Any time anyone resigns, it's—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You are talking about once he resigned you didn't want him to continue?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But as a manager, when anyone resigns, you have to decide whether you want that person continuing to work in the organisation, particularly in a role as senior as that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Marks, sorry, I misunderstood you. I thought you were saying you didn't want him to continue in the role prior to him resigning.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No. Once there was—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You mean after. Was that just for the balance of his fixed term contract?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: He would have had leave entitlements and other things as well that would have had to be paid out. It would be a combination. He had been at the organisation for quite some years. Those entitlements would have been paid out, as is normal.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I do have others.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You will need to put them on notice. I am conscious that we are more than four hours behind.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I have other questions. I will put them on notice.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you very much.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sure,.
