portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, I don't see anything in all these inquiries and estimates sessions which suggests this government is looking at a postal bank, or, rather, a bank for the post office—a Bank@Post expansion to provide additional revenue to post offices. Do you have any intention of developing Bank@Post with additional services?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, with regard to your reference to inquiries, those aren't inquiries of the government; they're Senate inquiries.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It dealt with the priority of inquiries.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I need to get the language right. Obviously, we will consider recommendations from Senate inquiries. Obviously, Australia Post is very cherished and very important, and we're very committed to ensuring the financial stability of Australia Post, but operational decisions are a matter for the CEO.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, as I said to the chair, this is about a bank. This is the topic. Your commitment to Australia Post will be seen through what you do with it, but I want to know whether you have any intention of developing Bank@Post.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Separate from Australia Post, do you mean?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Bank@Post—using post offices as banks.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think you're asking me about the operational decisions of Australia Post.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: This is a topic we have been pushing for a long time, as have others. The state Bank of North Dakota, for example, is the only bank in North America that's made a profit every year of its existence—every year. The bigger banks have fallen over. The Commonwealth Bank used to be the people's bank when it was formed by a Fisher Labor government in 1912. It provided competition to the major banks. It became the biggest bank because it provided better services. It would be very beneficial for the community, for the LPOs, for all Australians and for freedom. I've long been pushing it. It's successful in other countries—Japan, for example, and, I think, New Zealand. Are you doing anything to push an Australian bank?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Graham is seeking to—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, I can respond to that. The question is: are we going to create or are we interested in creating a formal bank, a full banking business? At this point in time, no, we are not. I believe that's also the view of government. As you say, there are other postal operators around the world that are a part of large banks—Japan Post, for example, the largest bank in Japan. That was so from its origins many, many years ago. The differences between providing over-the-counter basic service transactions that we provide today and becoming a full-service bank are monumental. Obviously, the vast majority of our network is licensees. Those licensees are not trained, professional banking people. There would be a significant need to upgrade the skills and upgrade the actual physical outlets, because a lot of these outlets are very, very small. But, at this point in time, there is no strategy for Australia Post to do anything other than provide an over-the-counter banking service, as we do through Bank@Post.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The history of the Commonwealth Bank, the first people's bank, is that Denison Miller was its first governor. He took the bank to be the top bank in the country, which kept the private banks honest and gave them competition. So it's no surprise, then, that both the Labor and the Liberal governments, since 1923 and Denison Miller's death, have dismantled that Commonwealth Bank and then flogged it off as a private bank. Is this because, in the last election cycle, Minister, the Labor Party took $4 million in donations from Australian banks who do not want Australia Post developing their banking service business?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Denison Miller, Mr Graham, started from scratch. He had nothing. He built it into the biggest bank in the country—and the best bank in the country. For the record, the Liberal Party took $7 million from Australian banks. So that explains why they did nothing to widen Bank@Post. One Nation will treat creating a people's bank as a matter of urgency and use Bank@Post—offer those services around Australia. The bank has successfully worked for the benefit of the country.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What was your policy, sorry? What is it?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: To establish a people's bank?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: A bank.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: How much is that going to cost?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Just like the Commonwealth Bank.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Okay.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: All the best for your retirement, Mr Graham.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'll be very quick. In relation to the document that we uncovered, Mr Graham, have there been any changes made to that plan? I'm aware that there's been an email sent to all licensed post offices in relation to the LPO reimagined program.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's correct. There have been some changes. As you know, there were two components in that document that were highlighted. One was regional Australia, and it invested an extra $30 million to sustain the existence of those post offices. That part of our program is one that we are continuing to support. The second part—
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Has that been delayed?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, it has not been delayed. We're still in consultation as to how we would execute the second component, but it has not been delayed. The second part, as you are aware, was to look at conducting a trial. We had done two previous, successful campaigns in relation to buybacks in metropolitan areas, and we were suggesting doing another trial to execute that. We've decided to put that trial on hold. We have a lot going on in the postal network at the moment, and we have decided that we will put that current trial on hold.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Why did you make that decision?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We have made that decision based on feedback that we have received. We made that decision based on the amount of activity that's going on in relation to our overall postal network and the amount of change it can absorb at any one time. The whole purpose of consultation is to provide that feedback and for us, as executives, to sit back and ascertain what the right way forward is. We certainly feel that continuing with the regional investment is appropriate at this time, but at this point in time, we have decided to put the buyback program—the trial that we were anticipating—on hold.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is that because that went down like a lead balloon?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, we received feedback. Actually, we ran that program twice before very successfully, so it did not go down like a lead balloon. We just felt that, at this point in time, it was not appropriate to execute that trial; therefore, we've put it on hold.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Have you entered into any formal agreement in relation to establishing postal services at pharmacies?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No formal agreement has been reached with the Pharmacy Guild or pharmacists. We have 127 post offices where we are in conjunction with pharmacies, and that's been in place for over 25 years with Australia Post.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, have you entered into any type of agreement whatsoever with the Pharmacy Guild—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There has been no agreement with the Pharmacy Guild—
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: or discussions—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, they're a partner of ours at 127 post offices, so we have ongoing dialogue with the Pharmacy Guild. We have ongoing dialogue with them in relation to other services we provide, like same-day delivery of pharmaceuticals to people who are stuck at home. We find that the feedback we have got from consumers in relation to those pharmacies that are in conjunction with the post office to be very positive, both for the consumer, because they can obviously go and get their pharmaceuticals as well as their mail and their parcels, and for the pharmacy, because they generate foot traffic.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Aren't you severely affecting the local post office if you're establishing a competing service at a pharmacy? I understand there have also been some reduced rates that are now payable for certain types of services as a result of that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, that's not correct, because these are not replacing existing pharmacies. These are where we have an opportunity. Coleambally is a good example, where the licensee decided to leave, so we approached the local pharmacy, who was interested in setting up initially a CPA and has now gone on to be a full LPO.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm just getting some confusing information about the nature of your agreement with the guild. Is there any type of agreement in any shape or form, formal or informal, or a memorandum of understanding with the guild or with any group of pharmacies?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No. There is no MOU in place. But, as I said, we have an ongoing relationship with pharmacies and therefore, through that, with the guild.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Can I ask for all correspondence between Australia Post and the Pharmacy Guild since 1 July last year?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I will take that on notice.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm also asking for all injury data that you hold. I am again reiterating that I'm seeking for that question to be answered.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We have provided you with the data that we have in relation to it.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, you haven't provided any—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Obviously, with a workforce of 65,000 people, that data is extensive.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, I'm seeking the information, Mr Graham. It's available in different parts of Australia Post. There are certain people who hold that information. As I wrote to you and raised concerns, I'm asking for that information and if it can be compiled and provided to the committee, please.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm happy to provide that.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Very quickly, I'm concerned about the fact that there may well be businesses which are operating as postal outlets which are also selling illegal tobacco. What is Australia Post doing about that?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, we take obviously a very strong view. We had, in the press last week, someone at one of our licensed post offices in Berowra Heights being arrested for selling illegal tobacco, and obviously the licence has been withdrawn from that individual. We have, I think, raised this before and certainly in questions from Senator Smith. It is a very difficult and challenging situation. If it comes to our attention that any post office is selling anything illegal—in this case, tobacco—then obviously their licence will be suspended and we will report them to the authorities.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Are there any such investigations underway? If so, how many?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not aware of any investigations. However, there is work that is done on an ongoing basis with the AFP. We, for example, had a successful prosecution by the AFP last year when there was a gang, for want of a better word, that was arrested that was dealing in the delivery of illegal tobacco, doing what we call dead drops—so these were houses they knew were empty—and delivering tobacco. Then they would come across later on and pick that up. We worked with the AFP in close cooperation, which resulted in the arrest of about 11 people. So we continually look for it, but it is a challenging situation, Senator. I agree.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thanks, Mr Graham. I'll have to leave it at that due to the time.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I have some very quick questions.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Smith.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Of course, I want to turn to the closure of the Innaloo post office. Thank you to Australia Post for responding by email to my various questions over the last month or so. Australia Post had a public consultation process that went for all of 16 days. Four of those were weekend days. During that consultation process, you received 24 responses—19 of them were online, and five of them were handwritten. But, since then, I've received 1,200 signatures on a petition opposed to the closure of the Innaloo post office. I'm just curious to know how robust your consultation, public survey, process is when you get 24 responses and I get, through the active work of local councillors, 1,200 signatures from local residents opposing the closure.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'll refer to my colleague Mr Bannister, who's directly involved with the retail network. It's fair to say that closing any post office is an emotional issue for those communities. I'm not surprised by the extent of the signatures that you have received. It's quite a common occurrence, but I'll refer to my colleague Mr Bannister, who's got all the detail.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Let me acknowledge the impact that a post office closure has on a community. These are difficult decisions, and they're not ones that we take lightly. The process that you refer to is an engagement process. It is more robust than it has ever been. But this is the first time we have run that new process, and we're constantly looking and learning—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, this is the test of the robustness of the process. I get 1,200 responses; you get 29.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I acknowledge that. What we did get, though, is feedback around how we could support the community with transition. That particular locality of Innaloo has eight post offices within five kilometres, the closest being around 1.95 kilometres away.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: And you know that because you've been to the Innaloo Post Office and seen it for yourself?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I have. I've been to the market. I spend time in all of the markets around the country, visiting licensees and our corporate post office teams. As I said, they're difficult decisions, and we weigh up a number of factors. We look at impact on community. You've got some feedback there, which we acknowledge. There are also commercial considerations. This is a high-profile shopping centre with escalating rent. These are things that we have to consider, based on the density of surrounding post offices. We've worked hard in our surrounding post office network. We have upgraded facilities with investment at both Karrinyup and Osborne Park DC, we've extended hours, and we've extended a number of our services at the surrounding post offices.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When I inquired with Australia Post about the various factors that were contributing to the closure of the Innaloo post office, rents were not mentioned. What can you tell me about the financial performance of the post office? When I asked that question, the very helpful Australia Post official declined to provide me with any sort of granularity around the financials. So, what's happening at Innaloo post office financially at a high level? You've mentioned rents.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It is a loss-making post office, or was a loss-making post office, with declining foot traffic. One of the things that we've done in transition is make a conscious decision to retain the PO boxes. That was one of the things that we were able to do to support the community with transition. That maintains a rental at that particular location. That is something that we wanted to do, despite the fact that we haven't maintained the full-service post office, and we're leaning on the surrounding facility. Each time we close a post office—again, let me acknowledge the impact on community, particularly the elderly and vulnerable—it does support the remaining post offices, including licensees, in the surrounding market.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When I was told about declining foot traffic, I was told that the decline was by 10 per cent. That did not sound like a very strong justification. What does that 10 per cent represent in terms of raw numbers of foot traffic into Innaloo?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Let me take that on notice, because I don't believe that that number accurately represents the decline over previous years. I want to ensure—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That is the number that was given to me in an email in an exchange between Australia Post staff that obviously report through to you, who was very helpful over the last month or so that I've been engaged in this issue. But '10 per cent decline in foot traffic' was the justification that was provided to me, which struck me as being—I don't know what the raw numbers were, but a 10 per cent decline did not to me sound like a very strong argument for closure.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In isolation, I would agree with you, but that may have been in the last 12 months. We probably would have found that that's been quite consistent. But we'll give you the details. I agree that that's an important data point that should be delivered to you.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: On 9 October, the City of Stirling, which is the local government area, wrote to you, and I think they're keen. They've not yet had a response, so if you could deal with that expeditiously, that would be much appreciated. And, Minister, they also wrote to Minister Wells, so could they have the courtesy of a response as well. I understand that the Australia Post board might be visiting Western Australia in the future.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We are, and we invited your good self. I know that it's a sitting week and that you can't attend. Again, I'll be over there for the board meeting and I'm happy to reach out personally and meet with the mayor and other constituents within the Innaloo area.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's very, very generous of you, and I will absolutely take you up on that. I will not be there, but I'll absolutely facilitate that. Thank you very much.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, Senator.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Twelve hundred—Senator Smith's consultation process. Australia Post's consultation process—just 24.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: On that note, we say thank you to the officials from Australia Post and the Australian Postal Corporation. Mr Graham, we wish you all the very best in your retirement.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you very much, Senator.
witness_position: Group Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
I'm now in a position to release the officials from Screen Australia. Thank you very much. I appreciate that. In light of the time and the fact that we will be concluding at 11, we are going to combine the officials of the department and Creative Australia for this last session to permit more efficient questioning. It will be a crowded table, I'm sure.

Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I appreciate the department and Creative Australia accommodating the slightly unorthodox combination of the two of you. In the ordinary course, I would call officers and I would also invite Mr Collette to make an opening statement. In the interest of time, if you have an opening statement, I ask that you table it. Is that okay, Mr Collette?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, of course.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you very much. We're very appreciative of that. I will now go to Senator Henderson.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
I just want to ask firstly about the government's broken promise regarding the production tax offset for the Australian film industry. I refer to the 2024 Budget Paper No. 2, page 152, which states:

The Government will also remove both the minimum length requirements for content and the above-the-line cap of 20 per cent of total qualifying production expenditure for the Producer Tax Offset.

It's been 2½ years. There's been no legislated budget measure. Can I get an update on why the government has not delivered this budget measure?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The timing of legislation, because it's in the Income Tax Assessment Act, is a matter for the Treasury. We don't have any say in when the—
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, but you would be working with Treasury in terms of progressing that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It was an election commitment.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: A budget—
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, a budget commitment—I'm getting tired—in 2024 in this portfolio, so could you please update the committee on why this has not progressed? Have you done all the work at your end? Who's at fault? Is the Treasurer sitting on his hands?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can't say anything more other than that the timing of legislation, because it's tax legislation, is a matter for the Treasury and the Treasurer. We don't have any control over the timing of tax legislation.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What representations have been made to Treasury to progress the legislation of this measure?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think it's fair to say we follow up with Treasury very frequently.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Through correspondence?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Through discussions with our contacts in the Treasury.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Have you made any representations, or has the minister, through various means about why this has been delayed for so long?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not aware of that; I would have to take that on notice.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When did the department last engage with Treasury on this matter?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure. I can ask my colleague to let us know.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'd have to take the exact date on notice, but it was very recently.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Could I ask for all correspondence between the department and Treasury in relation to this matter since 1 January to be tabled or provided on notice. I would be grateful. Minister, do you have any idea when this will be legislated?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you for the question. I can tell you that the government remains committed to removing the 20 per cent cap. As announced in the 2024 budget, the measure remains part of the government's legislative program. Obviously, the timing is subject to the broader legislative agenda, which I think we've discussed a few times today. The changes will be applied retrospectively from 1 July 2024, consistent with the original announcement, providing greater certainty for screen producers.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm just looking at a report saying that Australia is set to lose $30 million of film benefits and a thousand jobs, which will go to New Zealand, because of the failure to legislate this measure. I'm referring to an article in the Australian by Tim Douglas on 3 August 2026. This is potentially going to cost a thousand potential jobs going to New Zealand.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: As I've said—I've said this a few times before in relation to legislation—first of all, this is, I think, a matter of for Treasury. Is that right?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's correct.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They're appearing tomorrow. I think Senator Smith will be there. He can ask those questions on your behalf. We are continuing to progress it as a piece of legislation, and we look forward to your support to get it through the parliament in a timely manner, if that's the case.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: This is very embarrassing. Has Treasury indicated when it will be progressing this legislation? There are a thousand jobs on the line right now, Minister.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, I've answered your question. Treasury can provide you more information tomorrow because they are appearing and they are the relevant agency. We are still committed to delivering it.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The question I can ask the officials is: has Treasury indicated a timeline as to when this proposed legislation will be introduced into the parliament? Do you have any timeline?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Not that I'm aware, but we can take that on notice to request that.
witness_organisation: Department of Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications, Sport and the Arts
witness_position: Deputy Secretary, Creative Economy and the Arts Group

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Well, that's a very disappointing outcome for the film production sector in this country. Can I just quickly turn to the government's position on copyright for artists. We haven't got time to go through all the history and all the controversy about this matter. Will the government commit to not changing Australian copyright laws, which will protect artists and other creatives in this country?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text:
You would have seen public comments from the minister and also from the Prime Minister. I can repeat those comments for you if you like. The Prime Minister said, in a speech at the University of Sydney on 15 July:

Australian writers, musicians, artists and journalists must retain ownership and control of their work. Our laws will spell that out, plain as day. An artist's creative endeavour is their work and their property. No company should use Australian books, music, art or news to build or train AI without the artist's control. That includes the artist's control of the price and value of their work. Anything less, is theft.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Okay, but that didn't quite address my question. Will the government, as far as you are able to inform us, commit to not changing copyright laws in this country?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, that is the same answer to the question that you asked. If it assists you, responsibility for copyright sits with the Attorney-General. That department appeared yesterday. There were questions around copyright and AI throughout that committee. Of course, responsibility for the broader AI policy sits with the Minister for Industry and Innovation. He will be appearing later this week as well. The department of Minister Burke, who is now the relevant minister—I'm not representing the Minister for Communications anymore—are working to ensure that the creative sector's view is part of the conversation that we continue to have.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I appreciate which ministers have responsibility for what elements of this proposal, but I can assure you, Minister, that Australian musicians, producers, authors, artists and writers right across this sector are extremely concerned about the current debate and the suggestion that their copyright, their intellectual property rights, will be undermined by your government. I am not sure that what you've told me is sufficient to give them the certainty they need that their property will be their own to do with as they see fit.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, you have a habit of taking an answer that I give and turning it into something else. I can only answer this question the same way.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't think I do—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, you do.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: and I'm not reflecting on you personally.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's that you have an extraordinary ability to reframe answers into something else. I think that the Prime Minister's statement is very clear and unequivocal about the government's commitment to protecting artists and their work.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I won't continue with this because we are so short of time. I want to move to Creative Australia. Pearls and Irritations raised $669,240 through the Australian Cultural Fund for the promotion and presentation of arts and cultural activities. Mr Collette, good evening to you. What arts and cultural projects did Pearls and Irritations promise to undertake if it was provided with grants through the ACF?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They at the time met the eligibility conditions because parts of their publication—good evening, Senator. I'm sorry; I should have said that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's okay. I know things are rushed.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They run a number of book reviews, for example, and have critical reviews of creative work. The conversation has moved on, I can tell you, Senator, from the last time this was spoken about in Senate estimates. As you know, and as we've talked about before, we have reviewed the terms and conditions around eligibility for the Australian Cultural Fund over the last few months. It's a really important distinction here that Creative Australia is not the decision-maker. It's not like a normal grant. I know this is an obvious thing to say, but it goes to this whole issue of eligibility. Once we are satisfied that a program or an artist meets the eligibility criteria, which we have revised, we post that program or artist on the site, and it's actually the donor who decides whether they're going to support that program or artist.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I appreciate how it works.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So the amount of money that Pearls and Irritations have raised is not because we've made a decision. We've made a decision around eligibility, but it's because donors have decided—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No—I understand that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But, having said all that, in answer to your question: since we've reviewed our eligibility criteria to ensure that 100 per cent of the funds raised are invested in an arts and cultural program, we are not satisfied, as we sit here, that those eligibility criteria are being met by Pearls and Irritations—as we sit here.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Which is what I've been raising with you previously, in relation to the fact that they were not undertaking arts and cultural related activities in all respects.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Indeed. I take that point.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: But they are still taking the tax deduction.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Taking the tax deduction on money that donors have invested. We have had complaints, including your point. We took them seriously. We took a very close look at it, and we're now in active discussions with Pearls and Irritations about the way that that money has been spent and what it has been spent on. We've also met with the Australian Taxation Office to get further advice, and they are satisfied with the way we now define our eligibility terms in line with the tax act.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: In light of your revision, can I confirm that Pearls and Irritations no longer meets the eligibility criteria?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I can't go that far at this stage. We are in discussion with Pearls and Irritations, and, as you can imagine, those discussions still have to play out. We will make a final decision, but to speculate on that now could be prejudicial to those discussions.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So their eligibility for the Australian Cultural Fund is under threat—quite rightly, I would put to you—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We're reviewing it.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: because it was quite clear that this website and the other related activities were not concerned 100 per cent with arts and culture. There was a whole range of other activities.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We have sufficient reasons now to question Pearls and Irritations about how the money raised was invested. But, at the time that we agreed to post their programs, we were of course convinced that the money raised would be going to arts and cultural activity.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You did previously, very vigorously, defend their activities. Thank you for that update. How long will that review take? When will we know whether Pearls and Irritations will be able or not able to access these benefits through the tax office?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can't put a timeframe on it right now, but I can assure you that discussions are happening.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: What about those who are considering donating to Pearls and Irritations?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: They don't have a program live on the Cultural Fund site now.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's been taken down, has it?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It was completed, yes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Meaning they've got no current eligibility because there's no current program; is that right?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There's no active fundraising campaign at the moment on the website.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: When was that withdrawn or removed? Was that withdrawn or removed as a result of this investigation or review?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: No, I think it was completed.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It was completed on 14 December 2025.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Could we please have on notice the correspondence between yourselves, the department and any other party, including the ATO, about this matter, so we can properly understand the background and the details. We don't have a lot of time now to go through any more detail, so I look forward to receiving your—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson, I want to share the call with Senator Roberts in a couple of minutes.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Why don't you share the call with Senator Roberts. I've got a few more questions after that. Thank you.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Roberts.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you for appearing tonight. How much money did Creative Australia distribute by way of grants in the most recent financial year, please?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Our total investment was $301.4 million. It depends—and I'm not being evasive here—what you mean by a grant. Two-thirds of that sum is through government directed programs that agreed with the federal government but also with state governments and territories for the biggest programs that we run and invest in. That's the total package. We invested about $30 million.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Our grants expense in our 2026 annual report is $286.85 million.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is political persuasion a criteria to be considered when comparing the merits of any request for a grant from a group falling generally into the arts arena?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Not at all.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: The National Association for the Visual Arts has received funding from Creative Australia. How much was given to that group last financial year?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Creative Australia provides $229,522 per year to NAVA under a delivery path or investment agreement between 2025 and 2028. It's a four-year contract. NAVA receives its funding to provide important services and support to Australia's visual arts sector, which includes delivering the member insurance package and managing the visual arts code of practice, which sets appropriate fees for artists. As a national funded service organisation, we expect NAVA to deliver the services for which it is funded in a way that supports and is accessible to the full diversity of the visual arts sector. The answer to your question, Senator, is upwards of $229,000 a year.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You've also explained how the money was to be spent. Are you aware that NAVA—the National Association for the Visual Arts—members have been particularly vocal in their support of the Palestinian cause and supportive of the terror group Hamas, and have been particularly vocal in their negative views of the Jewish people and Jewish-Australians? Senior staff from this taxpayer subsidised visual arts body reposted online messages celebrating the October 7 terror attacks and massacre and dismissed concerns for Jewish safety. Are you aware of that?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I am aware of NAVA's published support the Palestinian cause. I am not aware of the level of detail you went into then about parts of it that it's critical of, but, to go to the substance of your question, as I said, as a national funded service organisation, we contract NAVA to provide services which we've agreed on to the full diversity of the visual arts sector. To that extent, we wrote to NAVA after some of these publications came to light seeking further information from them about the steps it's taking to address the concerns raised. We reinforced the importance of ensuring that all Australian artists and craft practitioners feel included and safe when engaging with Creative Australia funded service-delivery partners. Those discussions still continue.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: You're saying that this is not a good way for Australian tax dollars to be spent, I hope.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not saying exactly that. We're very clear about the services that we are contracting as a service-delivery partner. The assurance we want, given some of the statements that have been brought to light is that, as a membership organisation, NAVA will support—provide services—to the full range and diversity of Australian visual artists.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: On that, how many grants were provided by Creative Australia to Jewish creative groups in the last financial year?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can't answer that. I couldn't answer it on any religious faith or culture because we simply do not, as a point of principle, gather that information. It's not the reason that we would fund artists or artistic programs.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: So you probably can't answer, then, what the value of grants made by Creative Australia to Jewish creative groups in that period were either.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I can't answer that, no.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Is there an anomaly here? How do your eligibility criteria stack up now?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I don't think there's an anomaly. I can't, to my mind, see why there is an anomaly.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: It's okay to fund Hamas?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: We do not collect religious information or information about race or culture on any of the people who apply for grants or investment.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Surely you're not saying it's okay to support terrorists?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: That's not what the—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm certainly not.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: He's not saying that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not saying that.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson.

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Just on this matter, Mr Collette, in relation to the special envoy's recommendations that the government should not be providing funding to organisations that negatively impact social cohesion, including by promoting antisemitism—this is something that we've traversed a lot in recent times—what steps is Creative Australia taking to advance matters in this regard?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I assure you, Senator, we would never invest in an organisation—a service delivery organisation or a creative organisation—that is antisemitic in its views. We wouldn't do that. We are in discussion with—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, Mr Collette—you have done that, and we had a very extensive debate about that in relation to Mr Matt Chun at the last estimates at which you appeared. We haven't got time to traverse that, but you indicated that there were going to be some advancements made in relation to dealing with this matter. Has there been any progress made by Creative Australia in relation to the funding of organisations or those who undermine social cohesion?

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: There's been very significant progress in terms of how we are thinking about ensuring our processes are as good as they could be. Senator, you'll know that we appeared at the royal commission. We took that appearance very much to heart. We brought to the table there the kind of work we were doing to review our processes, and I could go through them in great detail. But I come back to my original point: we would never knowingly invest in an organisation or an artwork or an arts program that we considered to be Islamophobic or antisemitic or racist in any shape or form. Where we are with NAVA, to go back to that particular point, is that we've written to them, we are discussing our concerns that they provide services to the full diversity of artists without excluding any, and we will continue to have those discussions. And the reason we will do that is that, whenever there is an issue with an organisation we fund, we engage with that organisation and we try to make sure that our concerns are addressed, whether they're financial concerns for a performing company or—

portfolio: INFRASTRUCTURE, TRANSPORT, REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT, COMMUNICATIONS, SPORT AND THE ARTS PORTFOLIO
text: I think history shows a very different version. But I think that, to be fair, we'll need to pick this up at the next estimates. I have one final question to you.
